We consider a class of wireless powered devices employing Hybrid Automatic Repeat reQuest (HARQ) to ensure reliable end-to-end communications over a two-state time-varying channel. A receiver, with no power source, relies on the energy transferred by a Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT) enabled transmitter to receive and decode information. Under the two-state channel model, information is received at two different rates while it is only possible to harvest energy in one of the states. The receiver aims to decode its messages with minimum expected number of re-transmissions. Dynamic and continuous nature of the problem motivated us to use a novel Markovian framework to bypass the complexities plaguing the conventional approaches such as MDP. Using the theory of absorbing Markov chains, we show that there exists an optimal policy utilizing the incoming RF signal solely to harvest energy or to accumulate mutual information. Hence, we convert the original problem with continuous action and state space into an equivalent one with discrete state and action space. For independent and identically distributed channels, we prove the optimality of a simple-to-implement harvest-first-store-later type policy. However, for time-correlated channels, we demonstrate that statistical knowledge of the channel may significantly improve the performance over such policies.

This approach utilizes many of the desirable aspects from successful inverse dynamics based controllers in the literature, while also incorporating a variant of control Lyapunov functions that renders better convergence in the context of tracking outputs. We consider machine learning, particularly regression, using locally-differentially private datasets. The Wasserstein distance is used to define an ambiguity set centered at the empirical distribution of the dataset corrupted by local differential privacy noise. The ambiguity set is shown to contain the probability distribution of unperturbed, clean data. The radius of the ambiguity set is a function of the privacy budget, spread of the data, and the size of the problem. Hence, machine learning with locally-differentially private datasets can be rewritten as a distributionally-robust optimization. For general distributions, the distributionally-robust optimization problem can relaxed as a regularized machine learning problem with the Lipschitz constant of the machine learning model as a regularizer. For linear and logistic regression, this regularizer is the dual norm of the model parameters. For Gaussian data, the distributionally-robust optimization problem can be solved exactly to find an optimal regularizer. This approach results in an entirely new regularizer for training linear regression models. Training with this novel regularizer can be posed as a semi-definite program. Finally, the performance of the proposed distributionally-robust machine learning training is demonstrated on practical datasets.

After the fluid is converted to steam, it is used to spin a turbine, which powers a generator to make electricity. The steam is then condensed and returned to the heat exchanger, where it is heated by the earth. This process is repeated over and over again, in a closed loop. The last major schism had to do with the issue of whether the PCK should join the WCC. The controversy divided the PCK into two denominations, The Presbyterian Church of Korea (Tonghap, ) and The General Assembly of Presbyterian Church in Korea (Hapdong, ) in 1959. What difficulties and issues does women’s entrepreneurship face in the modern world? One of the main problems is the low availability of funding, as well as the weak viability of female startups, and the lack of growth (Alecchi, 2020). The key to solving these issues, according to researchers, is high-quality networking and the ease of access to the business community. Countries with easier access to the entrepreneurial community have smaller gender gaps in the performance and vitality of startups. Although many of the barriers that entrepreneurs face are common, women find it more difficult to overcome them. The main obstacles remain a lack of information, limited access to finance for starting a business, unfavorable tax policies, and difficult administrative procedures. Therefore, state policies should increase the economic opportunities of women by supporting those who start, formalize, or develop their businesses, as well as by integrating gender equality issues in the development of enterprises. I disagree with the principal's decision to require all students to participate in at least one extracurricular activity. While extracurriculars provide many benefits, mandating involvement prevents students from having true choices over how to spend their time. There are good reasons one might support extracurricular activities. They allow students to explore interests, learn skills beyond academics, and build resumes. Participating in sports, arts groups, or clubs is also a great way to relieve stress and stay engaged in school. However, forcing participation means some students will be involved in activities they do not truly care about or have passion for. This undermines the potential for reward and enrichment from such activities. Not all students have the time or ability to balance extracurriculars with academic demands and personal responsibilities. Some work part-time jobs to help support their families, care for siblings after school, or struggle balancing classwork with learning disabilities. For these students, an extra mandatory commitment could negatively impact their studies or mental health. Everyone learns and recharges in different ways for some, free time without additional pressures is essential. Rather than require acrosstheboard participation, a better policy would be to encourage involvement and make a variety of options accessible to all students. Those who want to get involved could receive support for choosing activities aligned with their goals and interests. For others, optional clubs and intramural programs would be available as a less stressful way to socialize and try new things. With genuine choices, all students have opportunities to thrive in or out of extracurricular activities as works best for their circumstances. Forced involvement helps no one and may unintentionally create more barriers to student success. Overall, this policy should be made optional rather than mandatory to respect differing needs and priorities.

Depleted uranium is also used as a shielding material in some containers used to store and transport radioactive materials. While the metal itself is radioactive, its high density makes it more effective than lead in halting radiation from strong sources such as radium. Other uses of depleted uranium include counterweights for aircraft control surfaces, as ballast for missile re-entry vehicles and as a shielding material. Due to its high density, this material is found in inertial guidance systems and in gyroscopic compasses. Depleted uranium is preferred over similarly dense metals due to its ability to be easily machined and cast as well as its relatively low cost. The main risk of exposure to depleted uranium is chemical poisoning by uranium oxide rather than radioactivity (uranium being only a weak alpha emitter).

In a passive PA system, the speakers and amplifiers are separate components that are connected by wires. The amplifier boosts the audio signal coming from the mixer or audio source, and sends it to the speakers, which then produce sound waves that we can hear. In an active PA system, the speakers and amplifiers are combined into one unit. This means that the amplifiers are built into the speakers, and there is no need for separate amplifiers. The audio signal from the mixer or audio source is sent directly to the active speakers, which amplify the signal and produce sound waves. In general, passive PA systems are more complex and require more setup, but they offer more flexibility and control over the sound. Active PA systems are simpler and more convenient, but they may not offer as much control over the sound.

Businesses have made increasing adoption and incorporation of cloud technology into internal processes in the last decade. The cloud-based deployment provides on-demand availability without active management. More recently, the concept of cloud-native application has been proposed and represents an invaluable step toward helping organizations develop software faster and update it more frequently to achieve dramatic business outcomes. Cloud-native is an approach to build and run applications that exploit the cloud computing delivery model's advantages. It is more about how applications are created and deployed than where. The container-based virtualization technology, e.g., Docker and Kubernetes, serves as the foundation for cloud-native applications. This paper investigates the performance of two popular computational-intensive applications, big data and deep learning, in a cloud-native environment. We analyze the system overhead and resource usage for these applications. Through extensive experiments, we show that the completion time reduces by up to 79.4 by changing the default setting and increases by up to 96.7 due to different resource management schemes on two platforms. Additionally, the resource release is delayed by up to 116.7 across different systems. Our work can guide developers, administrators, and researchers to better design and deploy their applications by selecting and configuring a hosting platform.

Ian Fleming's James Bond novels are iconic spy thrillers that capture the tense atmosphere of espionage during the Cold War era. Published in the 1950s and 60s, the books depict the Soviet Union as a sinister threat to Western democracy and follow the suave and skilled MI6 agent James Bond as he carries out dangerous missions across the globe. The antagonists in Fleming's novels are agents of SPECTRE, an international criminal organization, as well as the KGB, the main security agency of the Soviet Union. The plots frequently involve SPECTRE or the KGB plotting to steal secret information, sabotage Western infrastructure, or destabilize global politics. Bond is dispatched by MI6 to stop these plans and protect Britain's interests. The espionage depicted in the books highlights the paranoia and suspicion that permeated the Cold War, with constant worries about surveillance, defections, and double agents. Bond himself is the embodiment of Western ideals of masculinity and patriotism. He is sophisticated yet tough, equally comfortable in a casino as he is in a fistfight. Although he works with cutting-edge technology provided by Q Branch, his intelligence and physical skills are what truly make him a formidable spy. His suave and promiscuous lifestyle also reflects the aspirational qualities of masculine freedom and pleasure-seeking in postwar Britain. The exotic locations featured in the books, from the Jamaican tropics of Dr. No to the Japanese Alps of You Only Live Twice, also provide escapism for readers. The glamorous settings contrast with the gritty themes of espionage but also show how the Cold War intruded into even the most remote corners of the world. Fleming's vivid descriptions of cuisine, fashion, and scenery convey the sensations of travel at a time when foreign holidays were just becoming more common and accessible for Britons. Through the character of James Bond and the world of espionage, Ian Fleming captured the atmosphere of danger and moral ambiguity that defined the Cold War era. His thrillers explored the tensions between Western democracy and Soviet communism that gave rise to decades of covert operations and proxy wars. Although dated in their politics and view of women, the James Bond books remain highly entertaining spy classics that shaped popular culture.

Drivers Should Not Use Cell Phones in Any Capacity While Operating a Vehicle There are several strong arguments for why drivers should not be permitted to use cell phones in any capacity while driving. The top priority must be safety on the road, and all available evidence shows that cell phone use significantly increases risk of accident. When a person is driving, their full attention needs to be on the task at hand steering the vehicle, monitoring traffic conditions, and being aware of their surroundings. Any distraction pulls their focus away from safe driving. Talking or texting on a phone requires visual, manual, and cognitive attention that would otherwise be devoted to driving safely. Numerous studies have demonstrated that using a phone while driving leads to slower reaction times, failures to notice important road signs and signals, and increased risk of rear ending other vehicles or drifting into other lanes. Hands-free use of phones does not eliminate the cognitive distraction of a phone conversation. The brain can only focus on one complex task at a time, so participating in a phone discussion divides a driver's mental resources between two tasks. They may be less aware of what is happening around them on the road. Accident risk does not decrease just because both hands are on the wheel if the mind is still engaged with the phone call. Beyond safety concerns, allowing any phone use sets a poor example and can undermine traffic laws. When phones are even partially permitted, some drivers may push boundaries and engage in more dangerous behaviors like typing or browsing. It also sends a mixed message that would confuse other road users about what behaviors are and are not considered driving distractions. For the law to be clear and enforceable, a total ban on phones is necessary. In the end, no phone call or text is worth endangering oneself or others through an accident. With lives at stake each time someone gets behind the wheel, prohibiting all cell phone use is a reasonable restriction to prioritize safety on our roads. Drivers should focus their full attention on the critical task of safe vehicle operation without distractions. For these important reasons, cell phones should not be used in any form while driving.

Correlation and Causation Distinction Essay The distinction between correlation and causation is important because their relationship creates the ultimate base for critical thinking. Human minds work in a way that makes us search for mechanisms, consistent patterns, sequences, and regularities and then build assumptions. Such judgments are mainly generalizations founded on statistical data which helps us predict the future based on past experiences in several cases, but is not true in all of the situations. This means that each situation is individual and unique, and should not be evaluated based on assumptions. Instead, each case should be tested and researched objectively and a generalization should not be made without proper proof. The issue is that this proof is only available in such fields as Science, Physics, or Mechanics, while in History, Sociology or Philosophy it is impossible to collect enough data to completely exclude possibilities of all causes leaving just one to be true. This way, a certain level of generalization is always present. As a researcher, to make a study maximally objective and at the same time provide valid research, I would collect as much data as possible to prove my assumptions. Besides, since generalization and seeming causality based on correlation is often used as a basis for framing in politics and journalism I would be very careful making statements and drawing conclusions. An objective researcher is to prove the connections and always mention that even though there are certain regularities, the particular statistical data do not determine the causality between the two happenings with a 100 percent guarantee. In such a study data analysis and statistics should include both the patterns that prove causality and the ones that work against it. Only in this case, the study is fair and unbiased. Avoiding unfounded assumptions is vital for a highly qualified researcher working in any field. Observation of the correlation between various happenings is necessary, yet it does not allow the researchers to state that the correlated phenomena are in a causal relationship. An unbiased study provides the data and makes conclusions only to a certain extent.

Symbols in “Greenleaf” Story by Flannery O’Connor Essay To start with, Flannery O’Connor was an American novelist and story writer born in the 1925 year. In 1965, she published the book, consisting of several short stories, called “Everything That Rises Must Converge.” This book involves a piece of literature called “Greenleaf,” describing the story of Mrs. May, who experiences a conflict concerning social class struggle with Mr. Greenleaf, her employee, and two of his sons. At the beginning of the “Greenleaf” short story, Mrs. May has a dream where a bull destroys her life and the lives of her two unmarried sons. Interestingly enough, opposite to Mr. Greenleaf’s children, Mrs. May’s sons are not interested in farming, which their mother owns. Thus, children here can be considered a symbol: successful sons represent the happiness of Mr. Greenleaf’s life, while unwillingness to work and marry Mrs. May’s sons stands for the meaningless of her own life. Moreover, the crucial symbol in this story is a bull because he appears not only in the dream but also on the actual farm of Mrs. May. It turned out that Mr. Greenleaf’s sons are the owner of the bull that scares Mrs. May. When she realizes who is the owner of the scaring animal, she insists that Mr. Greanleaf should put the bull away from her farm or shoot it. At the end of the story, Mrs. May appears to be killed by this bull, which is ironic because it happens when the animal itself should be killed. Interestingly enough, the wife of Mr. Greenleaf was represented as a very religious woman who always prayed for Jesus attacking her heart to be pure from any sins. That is why, when Mrs. May becomes killed by the bull’s horns, one can see the animal as the symbol representing Jesus. To conclude, different symbols can be seen in Flannery O’Connor’s “Greenleaf” short story. Moreover, such symbolism opposes Mr. Greenleaf’s life to Mrs. May’s one, which raises the topic of social class struggle. The final scene, where the bull’s horns are killing the story’s main character as it was in her dream, stands for the idea of Jesus attacking the heart of Mr. Greenleaf’s very religious wife.

Data Reliability in Financial and Managerial Accounting Essay Both types of accounting requite accuracy of information, but there is a different degree of data reliability in the two of them. Financial accounting requires much more accuracy than managerial accounting does. There are several reasons for the need for precision in financial accounting data. The main cause for requiring accuracy in financial accounting is associated with the aim of such accounting. The reports on financial accounting are aimed to be analyzed by professionals or institutions from outside the organization in which they are prepared (Narayanaswamy, 2017). Therefore, it is of utmost importance to provide the most authentic data so as not to misguide anyone checking it. Another reason for the reliability of information in financial accounting is that usually, reports comprise data of a large period of time, which means that a small mistake or an inaccurate statement may undermine the dependability of the whole paper. Therefore, financial accounting is highly strict when it concerns the reliability of data used in the reports. In managerial accounting, the demand for information reliability is not as high as it is in financial accounting. Managerial accounting is aimed at preparing reports not for external but for internal use (Warren, Reeve, & Duchac, 2016). These papers are necessary to build the future perspectives rather than analyze past achievements and losses. As a result, the major requirement for the data mentioned in such reports is their relevance rather than accuracy. Therefore, it is necessary to keep in mind that both managerial and financial accounting presuppose accuracy, but they do not require it to the same extent. While in managerial accounting, the emphasis is put on data relevance, in financial accounting, the primary requirement to information is accuracy and reliability. References Narayanaswamy, R. (2017). Financial accounting: A managerial perspective (6th ed.). Delhi, India: PHI Learning Private Limited. Warren, C. S., Reeve, J. M., & Duchac, J. E. (2016). While distance learning offers some benefits of flexibility, attending regular unperson classes provides students with invaluable social and educational experiences that are difficult to replace. Some purported benefits of distance learning include greater flexibility in scheduling and the ability to learn from home. This could appeal to students who have scheduling conflicts or transportation difficulties getting to a physical school location every day. Distance learning may also save families money on transportation costs or enable a student to more easily keep up with classwork during absences. However, these benefits come at quite a cost in other areas of development. The social interactions that occur naturally in a traditional classroom setting are critical aspects of education. By attending class unperson, students learn how to communicate and cooperate with their peers. They build interpersonal skills through group projects, discussions, and casual interactions during class time. The social ponds and network of relationships formed in school often last for life. Distance learning replaces these spontaneous social opportunities with limited online interaction. Likewise, the educational experience suffers without a physical teacher present. While online lectures and course materials can convey academic content, the most impactful teaching involves personal guidance, discussions with the instructor, and lessons tailored to a class' needs at the moment. Subtle cues from students that help teachers assess comprehension are more difficult to detect remotely. Important guidance, feedback and mentoring happen organically before, during and after class through direct engagement between educators and learners. While distance learning fills a niche for some learners, for most students, attending regular unperson classes provides irreplaceable social and educational benefits that are important for their development into well rounded, socially skilled individuals. The interpersonal interactions cultivated in a physical school setting better serve students in the long run compared to a primarily isolated online learning experience. Overall, students are likely to benefit more from attending traditional classes versus relying mainly on distance learning from home.

When you copy a file, your computer is making a new copy of the file and storing it in a different place. This takes time because your computer has to read the entire file, and then write the entire file to a new location. When you move a file, your computer is just changing where the file is stored. It doesn't need to read or write the entire file, it just needs to change some information about where the file is located. This is much faster than copying a file. Imagine you have a book on your desk and you want to give a copy of the book to your friend. To make a copy of the book, you would have to read the entire book and write down everything you read. This would take a long time. But if you just wanted to give the book to your friend, you could just pick it up and hand it to them. This would be much faster than making a copy of the book.

As others have noted , translation is an extremely tricky business , and it 's pretty easy to introduce subtle changes in meaning ... but those differences can be important ( especially if you 're claiming that your book is The Actual , Infallible , Literal Word O ' God ) . For example , back in the 60s , US newspapers widely reported a story about Nikita Khrushchev shaking his fist and threatening the US by snarling , " we will bury you ! " But he did n't say that at all . What he said ( in Russian ) was closer to " we will be present at your funeral . " IOW , it was a boast : the mighty Soviet Union will be here long after decadent western capitalism has died . Not a threat . But that difference was used to drum up more war hysteria , and could have led the end of human life on Earth . In the case of the Bible , one word in particular has the potential to subtly change the meaning of a passage : thou . Today , that just sounds all Biblical and old - timey , but back when the KJV was produced , it had a more concrete meaning : it was the formal version of " you . " Many languages have formal and informal versions of " you , " which are used depending on whether you 're talking to a close friend or relative , or a stranger , your boss , or in some other formal setting . Thou was the English version of that , so if you translate a passage with " thou " to the modern English " you , " thou hast possibly introduced a subtle change in meaning . If the speaker is talking to somebody that they * should * use the formal thou , but say you instead , it carries the subtle connotation that the speaker is being rude or overly - forward .

Old Christmas lights are wired in a series circuit, which means that the electricity flows through each bulb and device within the circuit, one after the other. If one bulb goes out, it breaks the circuit and the electricity can no longer flow through the rest of the bulbs, which causes them all to turn off. New Christmas lights, on the other hand, are wired in a parallel circuit. This means that each individual bulb is connected directly to the power source and is not dependent on the other bulbs to be lit. If one bulb goes out, the others can still receive power and continue to stay lit.

Ranking data arises in a wide variety of application areas but remains difficult to model, learn from, and predict. Datasets often exhibit multimodality, intransitivity, or incomplete rankings - particularly when generated by humans - yet popular probabilistic models are often too rigid to capture such complexities. In this work we leverage recent progress on similar challenges in discrete choice modeling to form flexible and tractable choice-based models for ranking data. We study choice representations , maps from rankings (complete or top- k) to collections of choices, as a way of forming ranking models from choice models. We focus on the repeated selection ( R S) choice representation, first used to form the Plackett-Luce ranking model from the conditional multinomial logit choice model. We fully characterize, for a prime number of alternatives, the choice representations that admit ranking distributions with unit normalization, a desirably property that greatly simplifies maximum likelihood estimation. We further show that only specific minor variations on repeated selection exhibit this property. Our choice-based ranking models provide higher out-of-sample likelihood when compared to Plackett-Luce and Mallows models on a broad collection of ranking tasks including food preferences, ranked-choice elections, car racing, and search engine relevance tasks.

The Arches announced on Wednesday that it had gone into administration. Management said they had been left with no choice after a midnight closing time was imposed on its nightclub by the city's licensing board. The restriction followed police complaints about drug abuse and disorder. It was said to have cut total revenues at the Arches by more than 50, making it untenable as a business. Sandra White, the SNP MSP for Glasgow Kelvin, raised the plight of the venue at First Minister's Questions in the Scottish Parliament, where Deputy First Minister John Swinney was standing in for Nicola Sturgeon during her trip to the US. Ms White said 130 jobs had been put at risk by the Arches going into administration. She added: "Aside from the fact that the Arches is one of Glasgow's most cultural venues, this is obviously a very worrying time for the staff facing redundancy. "Can the deputy first minister assure those affected that the Scottish Government will offer all the support that it can?" Mr Swinney replied: "Creative Scotland is working hard with the organisation and with other partners to explore options regarding the future of arts programming of this nature in Glasgow. "Creative Scotland agreed with Glasgow Life and Glasgow City Council to bring forward some of this year's support for the Arches - PS92,000 from Creative Scotland and PS37,000 from Glasgow City Council - to assist with the delivery of the current arts programme in the short-term. "I reassure Sandra White that we will look in all ways that we possibly can do to assist in safeguarding the future of what I recognise as a significant cultural venue in the city of Glasgow and a venue that contributes a great deal to the cultural life of Scotland." Ms White said she was now calling on Glasgow City Council, Police Scotland and the management of the Arches to get round the table and "see what can be done to either reverse the closure or see what can be done to reopen the doors as soon as possible." The Scottish government has also said staff potentially affected the Arches going into administration would be supported through the Partnership Action for Continuing Employment (Pace) initiative. The Arches has received PS11.2m of public funding, including PS3.8m of capital funding, through Creative Scotland and previously the Scottish Arts Council over the past 20 years.

Critics of curfews argue that these rules may be counterproductive in some cases. For example, in places their curfews are strictly enforced, it can have a negative effect on the teen’s safety by causing them to flee from or avoid all enforcement during an emergency. In addition, it can over restrict teens, hampering their ability to develop healthy time management skills and even negatively impact their academic performance. Ultimately, it is up to parents and guardians to assess whether curfews are appropriate for their teens and HOL they should be implemented. When curfews are enforced properly and in moderation, they can be effective in promoting safety and instilling good habits and values in teens. Ultimately, curfews are just one of many tools available to parents and guardians to ensure their teens’ safety, wellbeing, and success.

Multi-output regression seeks to infer multiple latent functions using data from multiple groupssources while accounting for potential between-group similarities. In this paper, we consider multi-output regression under a weakly-supervised setting where a subset of data points from multiple groups are unlabeled. We use dependent Gaussian processes for multiple outputs constructed by convolutions with shared latent processes. We introduce hyperpriors for the multinomial probabilities of the unobserved labels and optimize the hyperparameters which we show improves estimation. We derive two variational bounds: (i) a modified variational bound for fast and stable convergence in model inference, (ii) a scalable variational bound that is amenable to stochastic optimization. We use experiments on synthetic and real-world data to show that the proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art models with more accurate estimation of multiple latent functions and unobserved labels.

Tymnet was an international data communications network headquartered in San Jose, CA that utilized virtual call packet switched technology and used X.25, SNASDLC, BSC and ASCII interfaces to connect host computers, front-end processors and terminal devices. Tymnet was a commercial product of Tymshare, Inc., a computer services company founded in 1964. Tymnet was the first major packet switching network to be deployed in the United States and one of the leading commercial networks in the world from the mid-1970s through the early 1990s. It was used by businesses, government agencies, military organizations, educational institutions and individual users for data communications. Its technology enabled customers to access remote resources, regardless of their physical location. Tymnet's proprietary protocol allowed it to provide higher levels of performance and reliability than X.25 networks and other competing products, making it an attractive choice for time-sensitive applications such as real-time financial transactions. The network was also equipped with a variety of security features to protect customer data. The network provided a wide range of services including file transfer, email, bulletin boards and interactive applications. In addition, Tymnet offered dedicated leased line services for large corporations and educational institutions. In 1989, Tymshare merged with McDonnell Douglas Information Systems Company, creating Tymnet Corporation. In 1994, Tymnet was acquired by British Telecom and subsequently merged into BT Field Services. In 1999, BT sold Tymnet to WorldCom, which changed its name to MCI in 2003. In 2006, MCI was acquired by Verizon Communications and Tymnet's operations were integrated into Verizon Business.

The use of the Series Elastic Actuator (SEA) system as an actuator system equipped with a compliant element has contributed not only to advances in human interacting robots but also to a wide range of improvements in the robotics area. Nevertheless, there are still limitations in its performance; the elastic spring that is adopted to provide compliance is considered to limit the actuator performance thus lowering the frequency bandwidth of forcetorque generation, and the bandwidth decreases even more when it is supposed to provide large torque. This weakness is in turn owing to the limitations of motor and motor drives such as torque and velocity limits. In this paper, mathematical tools to analyze the impact of these limitations on the performance of SEA as a transmission system are provided. A novel criterion called Maximum Torque Transmissibility (MTT) is defined to assess the ability of SEA to fully utilize maximum continuous motor torque. Moreover, an original frequency bandwidth concept, maximum torque frequency bandwidth, which can indicate the maximum frequency up to which the SEA can generate the maximum torque, is proposed based on the proposed MTT. The proposed MTT can be utilized as a unique criterion of the performance, and thus various design parameters including the load condition, mechanical design parameters, and controller parameters of a SEA can be evaluated with its use. Experimental results under various conditions verify that MTT can precisely indicate the limitation of the performance of SEA, and that it can be utilized to accurately analyze the limitation of the controller of SEA.

Digital inclusion refers to the ability of individuals and groups to access and use information and communication technologies. Social equity refers to providing fair access to opportunities and resources for all members of a community. There is a strong relationship between digital inclusion and social equity. In today's increasingly digital world, access to technology and the ability to use it effectively are crucial for full participation in society. Those without digital access or literacy are at risk of being left behind economically and socially. They may face barriers to accessing education, healthcare, employment opportunities, and more. Promoting digital inclusion is therefore key to achieving social equity and justice. Many marginalized groups face disproportionate barriers to digital inclusion. Those in poverty often cannot afford internet service or devices. Rural and remote communities frequently lack broadband infrastructure. Immigrants and refugees may be unfamiliar with the technology or language. People with disabilities can face accessibility challenges. And in many places, systemic biases and lack of opportunities have created a digital divide along lines of race, ethnicity, and gender. To achieve digital inclusion and social equity, we must work to provide affordable, high-quality internet access and tech devices for all. We need to offer digital literacy education and training, especially for marginalized groups. Governments and organizations should establish programs and policies to promote inclusion. They can also support the development of accessible technologies and digital tools for people with disabilities. Community technology centers that provide free access and education are helpful. Public libraries play an important role as well. There are many benefits to promoting digital inclusion. It can help disadvantaged groups access useful resources and information. It allows more people to take advantage of the educational and economic opportunities of the digital world. It fosters a more engaged, connected, and empowered society. And it strengthens the diversity of voices and experiences represented in technology and online spaces. In conclusion, digital inclusion and social equity are deeply linked. We must make efforts to provide access and opportunity for all people to use technology. Doing so will help create a more just, equitable, and prosperous society. It may take time, but working together, we can achieve the goal of universal digital inclusion.

Shiva is a period of mourning in the Jewish tradition that takes place after the death of a close relative. During Shiva, mourners typically observe certain customs and rituals to honor the deceased and provide support for one another.

Here are some common customs and rituals that are often observed during Shiva:

Mourners typically sit on low stools or benches and receive visitors who come to offer condolences.

It is customary for mourners to abstain from work, leisure activities, and other distractions during Shiva.

Mourners may recite the traditional Mourner's Kaddish, a prayer that praises God and expresses the belief in the eventual coming of the Messiah.

Mourners may also recite other traditional prayers and engage in Torah study as a way to find comfort and meaning during this difficult time.

It is also common for friends and family members to bring food to the mourners during Shiva, as they may not have the energy or inclination to prepare meals for themselves.

It is important to note that the specific customs and rituals observed during Shiva can vary somewhat depending on the individual and their community. It is always best to respect the wishes and traditions of the mourners and their family during this time of grieving.

Inbreeding is when two closely related individuals, such as siblings or cousins, have offspring together. This can lead to negative effects on the genetics of the offspring because the children are more likely to inherit the same genetic traits and defects from their parents. Imagine that you have a box of crayons with all different colors. If you choose two crayons from the same color family, like two shades of blue, and use them to draw a picture, the picture will likely be mostly blue. But if you mix crayons from different color families, like blue and yellow, you will get a picture with more variety of colors. In the same way, if two closely related individuals have a baby, the baby is more likely to inherit similar genetic traits and defects from both parents, which can lead to problems. For example, the baby might be more likely to have health problems, or might not grow and develop as well as a baby who has a more diverse mix of genetic traits. It's important to remember that inbreeding is not always harmful, and in some cases it can even have positive effects. However, in general, it is best to try to have a diverse mix of genetic traits in a population to ensure the health and well-being of the individuals.

The discovery of this once abundant species has led to a new research project by the California Academy of Sciences, which hopes to determine what happened to the seahorses and how they can be reintroduced to the area. Researchers are studying the behavior of other types of fish in the bay and looking for signs of seahorse life. The research team will also examine whether the introduction of artificial habitats, such as artificial reefs, could help the seahorses re-establish their presence in the bay. Artificial habitats can provide secure places for seahorses to breed and hide from predators. In addition to the research project, conservation groups are working to protect the remaining seahorse populations in the bay. They are encouraging local fishermen to use sustainable fishing practices and are advocating for better protection of the seahorse habitats. The disappearance of the seahorses from South Beach is a reminder of the fragility of marine ecosystems and the importance of protecting them. Hopefully, with increased awareness and conservation efforts, the seahorses will return to the bay.

I disagree with the principal's decision to mandate that all students participate in at least one extracurricular activity. While extracurricular activities can benefit students in various ways, forcing participation takes away student choice and autonomy. Not all students have the time or ability to take on extra commitments outside of schoolwork. There are several reasons why the principal's policy should not be implemented. First, some students need time after school for jobs, caring for family, or other responsibilities. Mandating extra activities does not consider students' lives outside of school and may place undue burden on those with limited time. Second, extracurricular activities require a commitment that some students simply cannot make due to other obligations or personal preferences. Students should have freedom to decide how to spend their afternoons and evenings. In addition, not all students have abilities or interests that align with available activity options. Forcing participation may cause stress, anxiety or low confidence for those unwilling or unable to join a team or club. It is unrealistic to expect that each student will find fulfillment in athletics, arts, academics or leadership. Individual strengths, weaknesses and priorities should be respected. While extracurriculars provide benefits for many students who freely choose to participate, mandating involvement denies student agency and diversity of needs and goals. An onesizefitsall policy disregards varied circumstances. Instead of requiring participation, the principal could encourage involvement and support students' choices through information about opportunities and their impacts. Dverall student wellbeing and self determination should be top priorities. For these reasons, I do not support the proposed policy of mandatory extracurricular activity for all students. Student choice and life demands both deserve respect.

The suspected green mamba was found on a ship that had docked in Aberdeen from west Africa last month. The snake died after it was placed in a freezer by the animal charity after attempts to rehome it with specialist reptile keepers failed. The snake was later identified as a harmless green tree snake. Police Scotland said a complaint was under consideration. Scottish SPCA Ch Supt Mike Flynn said: "We were called out after a green snake arrived in Aberdeen on a boat from Africa. "The snake was thought to be a green mamba, one of the deadliest snakes in the world. The snake was taken by police escort to our Aberdeenshire animal rescue and rehoming centre. "Sadly the snake, which staff genuinely believed to be a green mamba, had to be put to sleep after our attempts to rehome it to specialist reptile keepers were unsuccessful." He added: "We could not keep the snake in our centre due to severe health and safety concerns, as the closest anti-venom is held in Bedford. Green mambas also require a Dangerous Wild Animal Licence which the society does not have. "The safety of our staff and the public is paramount and as such the snake was placed in a freezer where it passed away. "The Scottish SPCA is proud of its policy not put healthy animals to sleep. Animals are only put to sleep on veterinary advice if they are too ill or too aggressive to be rehomed, or where we are legally required to do so. "The decision to euthanise the snake was not taken lightly. Unfortunately, the snake has since been identified as a harmless green tree snake. This has been an honest mistake on the society's part as we genuinely believed this was an extremely deadly snake." The western green mamba feeds on small animals and rodents and is mainly found in the coastal tropical rainforests of western Africa. Experts say its bite can be fatal in as little as 30 minutes.

They identified six basic facial action units (FAUs), which are groups of muscles that work together to produce specific facial expressions. These FAUs include the vertical lines of the eyebrows, the inner eyebrows, the outer eyebrows, the eyelids, the cheeks, and the lip corners. By using these FAUs, FACS allows researchers to encode different emotions and expressions into a system that can be easily replicated and analyzed. FACS has been used to study facial expressions in various contexts, including lie detection, emotion perception, and facial affective processing. For example, studies have shown that different FAUs are activated in response to different emotions, such as happiness, anger, and fear. By analyzing the activation patterns of these FAUs, researchers can gain insight into the underlying psychological states that underlie these emotions. FACS has also been used to study the neural mechanisms of facial expression processing. By recording brain activity using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), researchers can identify which regions of the brain are activated in response to different facial expressions. This information can help to identify the neural circuits that underlie facial expression processing and can be used to develop new interventions for disorders such as autism and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Facial action coding systems have been widely adopted in various fields and have become a valuable tool for studying human emotions and nonverbal communication. They have helped to clarify the complex relationship between facial expressions and underlying psychological states and have provided new insights into the neural mechanisms of facial expression processing. As a result, FACS has become an essential tool in the study of human emotions and nonverbal communication.

Title: Car-free Cities: A Sustainable Future? Introduction: In recent years, the idea of car-free cities has gained popularity as a potential solution to environmental issues and traffic congestion. The concept of completely eliminating personal automobiles from urban centers may seem far-fetched, but it could have numerous benefits for both residents and the planet. Main Body: 1. Reduced Emissions: One of the most significant advantages of car-free cities is the reduction in air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. Cities are responsible for approximately 70% of the world's energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, with vehicles being a significant contributor. By banning cars, cities could significantly reduce their carbon footprint, leading to healthier living conditions and improved overall air quality. 2. Better Public Health: Car-free cities would also lead to better public health. Reducing the number of automobiles on city streets would decrease traffic accidents and related fatalities. Additionally, the absence of pollution caused by vehicles would improve overall air quality. This would result in lower rates of respiratory and cardiovascular diseases, ultimately leading to a healthier population. 3. Enhanced Mobility and Accessibility: Car-free cities would prioritize pedestrian-friendly infrastructure, encouraging walking, cycling, and public transportation. This would promote physical activity, reducing obesity, and improving mental health. Furthermore, with fewer cars on the roads, public transportation would become more efficient, providing faster and more accessible transport for residents. 4. Improved Urban Design: By banning cars, urban planners could redesign city layouts to accommodate a more sustainable lifestyle. This may include wider pedestrian zones, bike lanes, green spaces, and more public amenities. These changes would create a more vibrant, people-centric environment that fosters social interaction, encouraging a sense of community and well-being. 5. Economic Benefits: A car-free city would require less infrastructure, such as parking spaces and roads dedicated to automobiles. This would result in significant cost savings for the city, allowing for the redistribution of funds to other essential services like education, healthcare, and public amenities. Additionally, the reduced reliance on personal vehicles would lead to less money spent on fuel, maintenance, and car ownership. Conclusion: Car-free cities may seem like a radical idea, but the potential benefits they could bring to both the environment and residents make them worth considering. While implementing this concept may not be feasible in every urban area, it could serve as a catalyst for sustainable urban design and a more people-focused future for our cities.

Working alone versus working in a group has both benefits and drawbacks. On the one hand, working alone allows for more independence and control over the work process. You can go at your own pace, make decisions without consulting others, and avoid any interpersonal conflicts that may arise from differences of opinion. However, working alone also means lacking the input and expertise of others. Group work, on the other hand, provides an opportunity to learn from others and gain new perspectives. Multiple people working together can also often achieve more than a single person. When working in a group, you have the advantage of being able to divide up the work. This makes complex projects more manageable as different people can focus on different tasks or parts of the project. Groups also have a wider range of knowledge, skills, and experiences that can be leveraged. Brainstorming together leads to more creative solutions as people build off each other's ideas. However, group work also introduces challenges that need to be navigated, like ensuring equitable workloads, overcoming communication issues, and resolving any conflicts between group members. There is also a risk of 'groupthink' where a desire for consensus overrides critical thinking. For many students, group work is a double-edged sword. On the one hand, working with peers provides an opportunity to develop important skills that will be useful for their future careers. Learning to collaborate with people from diverse backgrounds and work through differences of opinion are valuable life skills. However, group work also often introduces scheduling issues and a higher likelihood of 'free-riding' where some students do not contribute their fair share of work. When students are evaluated as a group rather than individually, this can lead to resentment if some students do not feel others contributed enough. In conclusion, while working alone and working in groups each have their pros and cons, both offer benefits that depend on the nature of the work and personal preferences. For complex or creative tasks, group work is often superior. But for work that requires deep focus or independence, working alone may be preferable. In many cases, combining individual and group work, for example by brainstorming together then dividing up the work to do separately, allows us to maximize the benefits of both approaches. The key is finding the right balance between working with others and working alone.

We present a method for learning an embedding that places images of humans in similar poses nearby. This embedding can be used as a direct method of comparing images based on their pose, enabling more accurate detection of human action in videos. We employ a feedforward neural network to learn a 2D embedding that maps images to a 2D Euclidean space, and show that the distances in this embedding correspond to the distances in pose space. We then use a novel nearest neighbors algorithm that takes advantage of the structure of the embedding to find poses similar to that of an input image. While technology that can identify human emotions has promising applications, using the Facial Action Coding System (FACS) technology to read students' emotional expressions in the classroom raises some concerns. On one hand, this technology could help teachers understand how their lessons are impacting students and adjust their teaching to better engage students. Knowing if students are confused, bored, or interested through facial expressions could guide lesson planning and methods. It may also help identify students who need additional academic or social-emotional support. However, constant monitoring of students' facial expressions also interferes with students' privacy and natural classroom experiences. Classrooms are meant to be learning environments, not laboratories for technological observation. Students should feel comfortable exploring new ideas and concepts without every reaction being recorded and analyzed. Facial expression analysis cannot determine the complex reasons behind a student's emotions and could lead teachers to make incorrect assumptions. Cultural and individual differences in expression may also not be properly interpreted. Rather than constant surveillance, teachers can regularly check in with students through less invasive means like quick polls or respectful conversations. With experience and empathy, good teachers can read a classroom reasonably well without technological aids. If issues arise, individual students can be privately consulted. While FACS technology may have uses, introducing it as a monitoring system in classrooms risks needlessly increasing student self-consciousness and compromising the human aspects of teaching and learning relationships. Overall, the potential downsides seem to outweigh the benefits in this specific application. Monitoring student emotions through facial analysis software should be avoided in classrooms.

Neural architecture search (NAS) enables researchers to automatically explore broad design spaces in order to improve efficiency of neural networks. This efficiency is especially important in the case of on-device deployment, where improvements in accuracy should be balanced out with computational demands of a model. In practice, performance metrics of model are computationally expensive to obtain. Previous work uses a proxy (e.g. number of operations) or a layer-wise measurement of neural network layers to estimate end-to-end hardware performance but the imprecise prediction diminishes the quality of NAS. To address this problem, we propose BRP-NAS, an efficient hardware-aware NAS enabled by an accurate performance predictor-based on graph convolutional network (GCN). What is more, we investigate prediction quality on different metrics and show that sample-efficiency of the predictor-based NAS can be improved by considering binary relations of models and an iterative data selection strategy. We show that our proposed method outperforms all prior methods on both NAS-Bench-101 and NAS-Bench-201. Finally, to raise awareness of the fact that accurate latency estimation is not a trivial task, we release LatBench - a latency dataset of NAS-Bench-201 models running on a broad range of devices.

The Electoral College has been a subject of controversy since its inception. While some argue that it is an outdated and undemocratic system, others believe that it is a stabilizing force in the representative democratic process of the United States. After reading the assigned articles, I believe that the Electoral College should be kept in place. One of the main reasons for retaining the Electoral College is that it ensures a certain outcome of the election. The winner-take-all approach used by most states ensures that the candidate with the most votes in that state wins all of the state's electoral votes. This eliminates the need for run-off elections, which can be time-consuming and costly. Another benefit of the Electoral College is that it requires candidates to have broad, transregional appeal. Candidates must appeal to voters in different regions of the country, rather than just focusing on densely populated areas. This helps to ensure that the interests of all Americans are represented in the election. The Electoral College also focuses attention on swing states, which are states where the outcome of the election is uncertain. This forces candidates to engage with voters in these states and address their concerns. Furthermore, the Electoral College balances the influence of large states. In a popular vote system, states with large populations would have a disproportionate influence on the election. The Electoral College helps to ensure that all states have an equal say in the outcome of the election. While some argue that the Electoral College is undemocratic, it is important to remember that the United States is not a direct democracy. The Founding Fathers created a system of representative democracy, and the Electoral College is a key component of that system. In conclusion, while the Electoral College may not be perfect, it is a stabilizing force in the representative democratic process of the United States. It ensures a certain outcome of the election, requires candidates to have broad appeal, focuses attention on swing states, balances the influence of large states, and avoids the need for run-off elections. I urge my state senator to support the retention of the Electoral College.

This signature is securely stored and can be used to verify the customer's identity when making purchases. One of the benefits of Amazon One is that it could potentially reduce the need for physical contact when paying for goods, which could be particularly useful during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, some people have raised concerns about the use of biometric data, particularly if it is hacked or stolen. Amazon has stated that it takes privacy and security seriously and that the palm signature data is encrypted and kept secure. Customers can also delete their palm signature if they no longer want to use Amazon One. At this time, it remains to be seen if Amazon One will be rolled out to more stores or if it will become a widespread payment method. There are three fields where you can put email addresses you want to send to . " To " , " Cc " and " Bcc " . " To " is for the people the message is intended for . This is very straight forward . " Cc " stands for " carbon copy " . Carbon copies were a way of making copies back in the old days . You put people in this field when you want them to see the message , but the message is not for them specifically . For example , I work with Bob , and I need him to do something . I send him a message saying , " Hey , Bob , can you do that thing I need ? " If he does n't get around to it , I can send another email saying " Hey , Bob , I really need that thing , " and I can put his boss 's email address in the Cc field . That way Bob gets the email , Bob 's boss gets the email , and Bob knows his boss got the email , so Bob knows his boss knows he needs to do that thing . The " Bcc " field stands for " blind carbon copy " . Let 's say I send a message to Bob , and put Sue in the Bcc field . Both Bob and Sue get the email , but unlike before , Bob can not see that the message also went to Sue . Sue gets a " carbon copy " but Bob is " blind " to that fact . Let 's say I 'm working with Bob again . Bob is being difficult , and I want * my * boss to know this . I send Bob an email , and I Bcc my boss . My boss gets to see that Bob is being difficult , but Bob does not know that I also sent this message to my boss . He thinks I just sent the message to him .

The rate-fixing scandal at Barclays involved the manipulation of an important financial benchmark called the "London Interbank Offered Rate" or LIBOR. This is the rate at which banks lend money to each other in the London financial market. It is used as a benchmark to set the interest rates on many types of loans, such as mortgages, credit card loans, and business loans. The scandal occurred when some employees at Barclays were found to have been dishonestly manipulating the LIBOR rate by submitting false information about the rate at which they were borrowing money. This allowed them to influence the overall rate and potentially make money for the bank or themselves. This is called rate-fixing and is illegal because it can harm other banks and companies that rely on the LIBOR rate to set the interest rates on their loans. It can also harm individual borrowers if the rate is manipulated in a way that affects the interest rates they pay on their loans.

In the 19th century, Africa was a continent that was largely under the rule of European powers. The Scramble for Africa had resulted in the partitioning of the continent among these powers, with many African nations becoming colonies. The indigenous people of these colonies were subjected to brutal exploitation and oppression by their colonial rulers. The anti-colonial independence movements in Africa were therefore formed with the goal of ending colonial rule and achieving self-governance for the African people. The strategies employed by the anti-colonial independence movements varied from country to country. Some movements, like the Mau Mau Uprising in Kenya, relied on armed resistance against colonial rule. Others, like the African National Congress (ANC) in South Africa, focused on nonviolent civil disobedience and protests. Still, others, such as the Rassemblement Démocratique Africain (RDA) in Algeria, adopted a mix of both violent and nonviolent tactics. Regardless of the strategy employed, all anti-colonial independence movements shared a common goal: to end colonial rule and establish an independent African state. They sought to achieve this by mobilizing the African people, both within and outside of the colonies, to resist colonial rule. This often involved forming alliances with other anti-colonial movements and seeking support from international organizations and governments. The outcomes of anti-colonial independence movements in Africa were mixed. Some movements, such as the ANC in South Africa, were ultimately successful in achieving their goals. Others, like the Mau Mau Uprising in Kenya, were brutally suppressed by colonial forces. However, the overall impact of these movements was significant. They helped to inspire a sense of national identity and unity among the African people, and they paved the way for the eventual decolonization of Africa. The anti-colonial independence movements in Africa were also important in shaping the political landscape of the continent. Many of the leaders of these movements went on to become prominent figures in post-colonial African politics, and the ideologies and strategies developed during the independence struggles continued to influence African politics for decades to come. In conclusion, the anti-colonial independence movements in Africa were a critical part of the struggle against colonialism. They sought to end colonial rule and establish independent African states, and they employed a variety of strategies to achieve these goals. While the outcomes of these movements varied, their impact on African history and politics was significant and enduring.

The facial action coding system (FACS) is a comprehensive coding system developed by Paul Ekman and Wallace V. Friesen that categorizes human facial expressions into six universal categories: happiness, sadness, anger, fear, surprise, and disgust. FACS uses a two-dimensional coding system that combines vertical and horizontal axes, with each axis consisting of six distinct categories. Each category is defined by a set of specific facial movements and expressions that convey the underlying emotion. FACS has been widely used in research, clinical settings, and marketing to study and interpret human emotions. It is often used to diagnose and treat mental health disorders, such as depression and anxiety. FACS has also been used in marketing research to identify consumer emotions and preferences. For example, FACS can be used to evaluate the effectiveness of advertisements and marketing campaigns by analyzing the facial expressions of consumers. One of the key advantages of FACS is its universality. The six emotional categories identified by FACS are observed across cultures and languages. This makes FACS a useful tool for cross-cultural communication and understanding. However, some critics argue that the system is limited in its ability to capture complex emotions and expressions that do not fit neatly into the six categories. Despite the limitations, FACS remains a valuable tool for understanding human emotions. Some schools offer distance learning as an option for students to attend classes from home by way of online or video conferencing. I believe that most students would benefit from being able to attend classes from home under certain circumstances. There are a few key benefits to distance learning. First, it provides flexibility that allows students to better manage their schedules. For example, students who have commitments like caring for family members or holding down a part-time job may find it easier to attend lectures from home rather than having to physically be at school every day. Distance learning takes away travel time and allows students to learn on their own schedule as long as coursework is completed. Second, attending classes virtually can improve focus and reduce distractions for some students. Being at home means students do not have to deal with the noise and activity that comes with a crowded school hallway between classes. They also have fewer social pressures that may take their attention away from what is being taught. The quiet, isolated environment of home learning could work better for concentrated study. However, distance learning is not right for every student or every subject. The social interaction and classroom discussions that occur face-to-face are important for many students. Some may also find it harder to stay motivated or maintain structure without the routine of physically going to school each day. Distance learning also does not transfer as well to hands-on subjects like labs, trades programs, or classes that require specialized equipment. In conclusion, while distance learning provides benefits like flexibility and a less distracting environment, it is not a perfect solution. It works best as an alternative option for students who need or prefer it, not as a replacement for traditional in-person classes. A hybrid model allowing both distance and in-person attendance maximizes benefits and accommodates different learning styles.

The AC-OPF problem is the key and challenging problem in the power system operation. When solving the AC-OPF problem, the feasibility issue is critical. In this paper, we develop an efficient Deep Neural Network (DNN) approach, DeepOPF , to ensure the feasibility of the generated solution. The idea is to train a DNN model to predict a set of independent operating variables, and then to directly compute the remaining dependable variables by solving the AC power flow equations. While this guarantees the power-flow balances, the principal difficulty lies in ensuring that the obtained solutions satisfy the operation limits of generations, voltages, and branch flow. We tackle this hurdle by employing a penalty approach in training the DNN. As the penalty gradients make the common first-order gradient-based algorithms prohibited due to the hardness of obtaining an explicit-form expression of the penalty gradients, we further apply a zero-order optimization technique to design the training algorithm to address the critical issue. The simulation results of the IEEE test case demonstrate the effectiveness of the penalty approach. Also, they show that DeepOPF can speed up the computing time by one order of magnitude compared to a state-of-the-art solver, at the expense of minor optimality loss.

Gibbs sampling is a Markov chain Monte Carlo method that is often used for learning and inference on graphical models. Minibatching, in which a small random subset of the graph is used at each iteration, can help make Gibbs sampling scale to large graphical models by reducing its computational cost. In this paper, we propose a new auxiliary-variable minibatched Gibbs sampling method, Poisson-minibatching Gibbs , which both produces unbiased samples and has a theoretical guarantee on its convergence rate. In comparison to previous minibatched Gibbs algorithms, Poisson-minibatching Gibbs supports fast sampling from continuous state spaces and avoids the need for a Metropolis-Hastings correction on discrete state spaces. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on multiple applications and in comparison with both plain Gibbs and previous minibatched methods.

Presidential candidate Andrew Jackson was the first Democrat ever to be associated with the donkey symbol . His opponents during the election of 1828 tried to label him a " jackass " for his populist beliefs and slogan , " Let the people rule . " Jackson was entertained by the notion and ended up using it to his advantage on his campaign posters . But cartoonist Thomas Nast is credited with making the donkey the recognized symbol of the Democratic Party . It first appeared in a cartoon in Harper 's Weekly in 1870 , and was supposed to represent an anti - Civil War faction . But the public was immediately taken by it and by 1880 it had already become the unofficial symbol of the party . Political cartoonist Thomas Nast was also responsible for the Republican Party elephant . In a cartoon that appeared in Harper 's Weekly in 1874 , Nast drew a donkey clothed in lion 's skin , scaring away all the animals at the zoo . One of those animals , the elephant , was labeled " The Republican Vote . " That 's all it took for the elephant to become associated with the Republican Party . They became a mainstay in the American political system when they played the role of economizing devices at the polls . In the late 19th Century when literacy rates were low , a symbol representing a party and its associated platform was easier to rally behind than a complicated , written party name or a platform . Instead of trying to decipher " REPUBLICAN " , illiterate American voters would just check the elephant instead .

Ethical questions abound about how computers should respond in split second situations involving loss of life. And widespread adoption could displace millions of jobs that rely on human vehicle operation. Rather than rushing development, policymakers and companies would be wise to thoroughly test driverless technologies through pilot programs first. Humans must stay engaged as a failsafe to handle unexpected scenarios outside of algorithms' training. Any deployment should happen gradually, car by car, as knowledge improves. Overall safety and social consequences should tame priority over profit or popularity considerations. Driverless cars offer promise, but also problems not yet solved. A prudent path forward is comprehensive research, rigorous testing, and cautious adoption not abandonment of human oversight before the technology proves truly ready to drive itself. With care and oversight rather than carelessness or haste, autonomous vehicles may someday transform transportation for the better. But getting there will require balancing innovation and caution at every step.

Most annelids have a pair of coelomata (body cavities) in each segment, separated from other segments by septa and from each other by vertical mesenteries. Each septum forms a sandwich with connective tissue in the middle and mesothelium (membrane that serves as a lining) from the preceding and following segments on either side. Each mesentery is similar except that the mesothelium is the lining of each of the pair of coelomata, and the blood vessels and, in polychaetes, the main nerve cords are embedded in it. The mesothelium is made of modified epitheliomuscular cells; in other words, their bodies form part of the epithelium but their bases extend to form muscle fibers in the body wall. The mesothelium may also form radial and circular muscles on the septa, and circular muscles around the blood vessels and gut. Parts of the mesothelium, especially on the outside of the gut, may also form chloragogen cells that perform similar functions to the livers of vertebrates: producing and storing glycogen and fat; producing the oxygen-carrier hemoglobin; breaking down proteins; and turning nitrogenous waste products into ammonia and urea to be excreted.

In many high level vision applications such as tracking and surveillance, background estimation is a fundamental step. In the past, background estimation was usually based on low level hand-crafted features such as raw color components, gradients, or local binary patterns. These existing algorithms observe performance degradation in the presence of various challenges such as dynamic backgrounds, photo-metric variations, camera jitter, and shadows. To handle these challenges for the purpose of accurate background estimation, we propose a unified method based on Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) and image inpainting. It is an unsupervised visual feature learning hybrid GAN based on context prediction. It is followed by a semantic inpainting network for texture optimization. We also propose a solution of arbitrary region inpainting by using center region inpainting and Poisson blending. The proposed algorithm is compared with the existing algorithms for background estimation on SBM.net dataset and for foreground segmentation on CDnet 2014 dataset. The proposed algorithm has outperformed the compared methods with significant margin.

The input color image is the underwater image while the output color image is the corresponding ground-truth, a dry image. By training on a large dataset of pairs of underwater and dry images, our method learns to correct the color in the input image, by minimizing a loss function computed over the pixels of both images. Encoding a sequence of observations is an essential task with many applications. The encoding can become highly efficient when the observations are generated by a dynamical system. A dynamical system is a mathematical model that describes the evolution of a system over time. It consists of a set of rules, often in the form of equations, that specify how the system's state changes as time passes. When the observations are generated by a dynamical system, we can take advantage of this underlying structure to create an efficient encoding. One common approach is to use a technique called symbolic dynamics. Symbolic dynamics converts the continuous time series of observations into a discrete sequence of symbols. The symbols represent different states of the dynamical system. By using this representation, we can analyze the properties of the system and make predictions about its behavior. Another approach is to use techniques from information theory to quantify the amount of information contained in the observations. For example, we can use entropy to measure the amount of uncertainty in the observations, and use compression algorithms to reduce the amount of data needed to represent the observations. The encoding of observations generated by dynamical systems has applications in a wide range of fields, including physics, biology, engineering, and finance. For example, in chaotic systems, the encoding can be used to identify the underlying attractor and extract useful features for prediction or control. In financial time series, the encoding can be used to identify patterns and predict future behavior.

In this paper, we develop a Bayesian evidence maximization framework to solve the sparse non-negative least squares problem (S-NNLS). We introduce a family of scale mixtures referred as to Rectified Inverse Gaussian (RIG) prior for the sparse NNLS model. We show that the proposed RIG prior is mathematically appealing and allows us to develop an efficient MCMC sampling algorithm for solving the resulting S-NNLS problem. We also show that our RIG prior based on Bayesian evidence maximization approach is mathematically equivalent to the recently proposed scale mixture based iterative reweighted least squares (SMIR-WLS) method for sparse NNLS. However, the proposed RIG prior has two distinct advantages over the recently proposed SMIR-WLS method. First, the RIG prior based Bayesian approach provides a principled framework for tuning parameter selection in a Bayesian manner by maximizing the marginal likelihood. Second, the Bayesian evidence maximization approach provides an easy and efficient MCMC sampling algorithm for solving the resulting S-NNLS problem. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed RIG prior based Bayesian evidence maximization approach via extensive experimental results on simulated and real-world datasets.
