Main body Planned internal changes might be considered a tactical move to transform the nature of the organization or the manner in which it conducts business. This may be either through varying the products or services, changing the organized structure, or expanding the size of the business (Bayerl, Lauche, & Carolyn, 2016). Several aspects such as technological innovation and improvements in communication and information networks are external in nature but may be implemented in a business in a planned manner to facilitate its success and boost overall productivity. Unplanned internal changes may be considered the reforms that occur in a firm without having been premeditated and are not strategic interventions. In most instances, unplanned internal changes happen in reaction to either a variation in the demographic constitution of a firm or are attributable to performance gaps (Kunisch, Menz, & Ambos, 2015). On the other hand, vital external aspects such as economic uncertainties and modification of government directives have a critical role to play in obliging organizations to undergo unplanned changes. Conclusion The management of change in the organization acts as an imperative pre-requisite for the achievement of competitive benefit and switching from the current situation of practice to a required futuristic mode of operation. That's actually an artefact of the recording process. Since we only capture a certain number of frames each second, if there's, for example, a clock face with the minute hand spinning around extremely fast, then if it's moving at just under once around every second, and we're recording at 60 frames per second, then every time the camera records the scene, the minute hand will be slightly before where it was the previous frame, since after the picture it spins all the way around again until just before its current position which is right when the camera is ready to take another picture. Imagine taking one photograph every second. If you are walking around in a circle, but are walking that circle in just under one second, then every time the photo is taken it'll be just before you reach the point you were in when the photo was last taken. If you put all of these photographs together one after the other, you'll appear to be moving backwards, because the parts where you walked all the way around are missing, and so when we watch an animation of those photographs, we assume you were just walking backwards and taking the photos more rapidly.

On balance, I am cautiously supportive of their continued development for several key reasons. One of the primary benefits outlined in the article is improved transportation access for those unable to drive themselves, such as the elderly or disabled. By removing the need for a human operator, driverless vehicles could grant independence and mobility to many people. This is an important humanitarian benefit. Additionally, the article notes these vehicles could significantly reduce traffic accidents caused by human error, given their reliance on sensor technology rather than fallible human judgment in critical situations. The societal impacts of fewer injuries and deaths on our roads are difficult to overstate. However, the article also raises some valid concerns. Autonomous systems driven by computer code are still far from infallible, and unanticipated errors or malfunctions could potentially put lives at risk. Yurthermore, ongoing development and testing of this new technology will require careful oversight and regulation to protect users and bystanders alike. Public acceptance may also lag behind the pace of innovation if safety risks are not adequately addressed and mitigated through partnerships with government. While driverless cars present both opportunities and challenges, on balance the societal benefits of improved mobility and road safety seem to outweigh the risks if this technology progresses carefully, transparently and adheres to high ethical standards of user and public protection. With appropriate safeguards, thoughtful policymaking and continued public discourse on these issues, autonomous vehicles may ultimately transform transportation for the better. Overall, done right, driverless cars could be a promising development.

Due to development of technology, linear controllers cannot satisfy requirements of high-tech industry. One solution is using nonlinear controllers such as reset elements to overcome this big barrier. In literature, the Constant in gain Lead in phase (CgLp) compensator is a novel reset element developed to overcome the inherent linear controller limitations. However, a tuning guideline for these controllers has not been proposed so far. In this paper, a recently developed method named higher-order sinusoidal input describing function (HOSIDF), which gives deeper insight into the frequency behaviour of non-linear controllers compared to sinusoidal input describing function (DF), is used to obtain a straight-forward tuning method for CgLp compensators. In this respect, comparative analyses on tracking performance of these compensators are carried out. Based on these analyses, tuning guidelines for CgLp compensators are developed and validated on a high-tech precision positioning stage. The results show the effectiveness of the developed tuning method.

Soft computing is a field of study that focuses on the design and development of computational systems and algorithms that are inspired by, or mimic, human cognition, perception, and behavior. These systems and algorithms are often referred to as "soft" because they are designed to be flexible, adaptable, and tolerant of uncertainty, imprecision, and partial truth. Soft computing approaches differ from traditional "hard" computing approaches in that they are designed to handle complex, ill-defined, or poorly understood problems, as well as to process data that is noisy, incomplete, or uncertain. Soft computing techniques include a wide range of methods, including artificial neural networks, fuzzy logic, evolutionary algorithms, probabilistic reasoning, and machine learning, among others. Soft computing techniques are widely used in a variety of applications, including pattern recognition, data mining, image processing, natural language processing, and control systems, among others. They are particularly useful for tasks that involve dealing with incomplete or ambiguous information, or that require the ability to adapt and learn from experience.

The Role of Art in Promoting Mental Health and Well-being Mental health is a critical aspect of overall well-being that often goes overlooked. It encompasses our emotional, psychological, and social well-being. Mental health issues can range from mild anxiety to severe depression, and can have a profound impact on an individual's daily life. Fortunately, there are various ways to promote mental health and well-being, including engaging in artistic activities. This paper will discuss the role of art in promoting mental health and well-being, the benefits of art therapy, and how art can be incorporated into daily life to improve mental health. The role of art in promoting mental health and well-being is multifaceted. Art has the ability to provide a sense of escape from the stresses of daily life, allowing individuals to engage in a creative outlet that can be both therapeutic and enjoyable. Additionally, art can help individuals express their emotions, which can be cathartic and lead to a greater understanding of their feelings. Moreover, art has been shown to increase confidence and self-esteem, which are crucial components of mental health. One of the most effective ways to promote mental health through art is through art therapy. Art therapy is a form of psychotherapy that uses art as a means of expression and reflection. It can be beneficial for individuals struggling with a wide range of mental health issues, including anxiety, depression, trauma, and addiction. The process of creating art can help individuals express their feelings in a safe and non-judgmental environment, which can lead to increased self-awareness and emotional regulation. Incorporating art into daily life can also have a positive impact on mental health. This can be achieved through activities such as painting, drawing, sculpting, or even simple acts like coloring or doodling. These activities can help individuals relax, reduce stress, and improve their mood. Additionally, engaging in artistic activities can provide a sense of accomplishment and enjoyment, which can boost self-esteem and confidence. In conclusion, the role of art in promoting mental health and well-being is significant. Art therapy can be a powerful tool for individuals struggling with mental health issues, while incorporating art into daily life can help improve overall mental health and well-being. Encouraging individuals to engage in artistic activities can lead to a more fulfilling and balanced life, ultimately contributing to a healthier society as a whole.

The cultural value of engaging with museums and art galleries is unquestionable; they exert a great deal of influence on our perception of the world. It is only reasonable to ponder whether or not these outlets of culture should concentrate their efforts on presenting the nation’s own art, and not that of other countries. In my opinion, there should be an attempt to strike a balance and put the objects of national art in the spotlight, while allowing the public to get acquainted with foreign artworks to a certain extent.If people were to only find sculptures and paintings by national artists in their local museums, that would have a number of positive effects, such as the fame the artists of that country would gain and the pride its citizens would feel for their fellow countrymen. It would promote patriotism and strengthen the image of the country in the eyes of its inhabitants. Local artists would also receive more financial assistance from the government as their works would generate a significant amount of interest, potentially resulting in further development of the local art. However, in order to evolve art needs fresh ideas, and without exposure to a wider range of creativity the world provides, the evolution of local arts may be hindered.People enjoy art because it appeals to their inner sense of beauty and triggers strong emotions, and whether the masterpiece that causes these feelings belongs to a local or foreign artist is irrelevant. Talent knows no geographical boundaries; therefore, the emphasis should be on how much joy or amazement the work of art brings, rather than on its origin. If that principle were to be followed, we would never have to choose between local and international art. Reducing our museums or galleries’ collections to local art works, in my view, would be harmful and go against the democratic nature of art.To sum up, it seems to me that a country has nothing to lose by allowing its people to admire art created elsewhere in the world. A conscious choice by the government to support local artists while hosting exhibitions from other countries could prove the most beneficial.

Articles 46-53 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties set out the only ways that treaties can be invalidated - considered unenforceable and void under international law. A treaty will be invalidated due to either the circumstances by which a state party joined the treaty, or due to the content of the treaty itself. Invalidation is separate from withdrawal, suspension, or termination (addressed above), which all involve an alteration in the consent of the parties of a previously valid treaty rather than the invalidation of that consent in the first place.

Online classes, also known as cyber school or virtual school, have become a popular option for high school students in recent years. While some students thrive in this environment, others struggle to find the same level of engagement and academic rigor as traditional brick-and-mortar schools. In this essay, I will explore whether online classes offer an appropriate educational experience for high school students. On the one hand, online classes offer several benefits for high school students. For example, students can take classes from the comfort of their own homes, which can be especially helpful for those who have busy schedules or who live far away from their school. This flexibility can also be beneficial for students who have difficulty with traditional school schedules due to health issues or other personal circumstances. Additionally, online classes can provide students with access to a wider range of courses and resources than what may be available at their traditional school. On the other hand, there are several drawbacks to online classes. For instance, students may struggle with the lack of face-to-face interaction with their teachers and peers. This can make it more difficult for students to build relationships and get the support they need to succeed academically. Additionally, online classes may not provide the same level of structure and accountability as traditional school, which can lead to students falling behind or not completing their work. In my opinion, online classes can be a good option for some high school students, but they are not appropriate for everyone. Students who are self-motivated and disciplined, and who have a good support system at home, may find online classes to be a good fit. However, students who struggle with organization and time management, or who rely heavily on face-to-face interaction with their teachers and peers, may find online classes to be less effective. In conclusion, while online classes can offer some benefits for high school students, they are not a one-size-fits-all solution. Students and parents should carefully consider the pros and cons of online classes before making a decision. Ultimately, the most important thing is for students to find an educational environment that works best for them and allows them to reach their full potential.

This paper presents a control reconfiguration approach to improve the performance of two classes of dynamical systems. Motivated by recent research on re-engineering cyber-physical systems, we propose a three-step control retrofit procedure. First, we reverse-engineer a dynamical system to dig out an optimization problem it actually solves. Second, we forward-engineer the system by applying a corresponding faster algorithm to solve this optimization problem. Finally, by comparing the original and accelerated dynamics, we obtain the implementation of the redesigned part (i.e., the extra dynamics). As a result, the convergence ratespeed or transient behavior of the given system can be improved while the system control structure maintains. Three practical applications in the two different classes of target systems, including consensus in multi-agent systems, Internet congestion control and distributed proportional-integral (PI) control, show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Annuities, like life insurance, are sold rather than bought. Once upon a time, IRAs inherited from a non-spouse required the beneficiary to (a) take all the money out within 5 years, or (b) choose to receive the value of the IRA at the time of the IRA owner's death in equal installments over the expected lifetime of the beneficiary. If the latter option was chosen, the IRA custodian issued the fixed-term annuity in return for the IRA assets. If the IRA was invested in (say) 15000 shares of IBM stock, that stock would then belong to the IRA custodian who was obligated to pay $x per year to the beneficiary for the next 23 years (say). There was no investment any more that could be transferred to another broker, or be sold and the proceeds invested in Facebook stock (say). Nor was the custodian under any obligation to do anything except pay $x per year to the beneficiary for the 23 years. Financial planners loved to get at this money under the old IRA rules by suggesting that if all the IRA money were taken out and invested in stocks or mutual funds through their company, the company would pay a guaranteed $y per year, would pay more than $y in each year that the investments did well, would continue payment until the beneficiary died (or till the death of the beneficiary or beneficiary's spouse - whoever died later), and would return the entire sum invested (less payouts already made, of course) in case of premature death. $y typically would be a little larger than $x too, because it factored in some earnings of the investment over the years. So what was not to like? Of course, the commissions earned by the planner and the lousy mutual funds and the huge surrender charges were always glossed over.

This paper introduces the variational Renyi bound (VR) that extends traditional variational inference to Renyi's a -divergences. This new family of variational methods unifies a number of existing approaches, and allows a novel class of tight lower bounds to the Renyi divergences. We show that a major hurdle to using the VR bound is that, for high Renyi orders, the bound is expressed as a maximization over a non-convex objective. We show that this optimization is solved efficiently and exactly by first-order methods, and present an efficient primal-dual algorithm for finding the global optimum. Finally, we provide experimental results on both synthetic and real data that show that our algorithm obtains significantly tighter Renyi bounds than existing methods.

Seeking multiple opinions when asking for advice can help someone make a better choice for a few key reasons. First, getting perspectives from different people exposes you to more information and viewpoints about your situation and potential options. No single person can possibly have all the answers or think of everything, so hearing from multiple sources helps ensure more factors are considered before deciding. Different people also have varied backgrounds, experiences, and areas of expertise that could provide unique insights. What might be an obvious solution to one person could be overlooked by another. Collecting advice from individuals with diverse backgrounds increases the chances of an aspect that particularly suits your needs being pointed out. As the saying goes, "two heads are better than one." Another benefit is that getting multiple opinions helps balance out potential biases. Any one adviser may unintentionally steer you a certain way due to their own preferences or situations. However, seeking advice from more than one person provides balance, as biases in one adviser's input could be counteracted by another's advice. This average of input helps lead to a more well-rounded recommendation. Lastly, comparing the advice received across multiple sources allows you to check for consistency and identify where the majority of suggestions align or differ. Areas that multiple advisers independently point out increase in importance and relevance to your decision. Differences of opinion also signal aspects that require more careful consideration from all angles before deciding on a course of action. Weighing various aligned and differing perspectives ultimately empowers the person seeking advice to make a choice they are confident is best supported. In summary, collecting advice from a few trusted sources, rather than relying on just one opinion, increases the chances of making a decision that takes full advantage of the collective knowledge, experiences and viewpoints available. It leads to choices being made with a more well-rounded understanding of all sides.

Finally, to address the highly dynamic nature of graph-based applications, researchers have proposed various dynamic scheduling techniques such as work-stealing and load balancing to distribute computation across processing cores efficiently. Overall, the challenges of implementing graph algorithms on parallel hardware such as GPUs are significant, but ongoing research has resulted in promising solutions that are improving the scalability and efficiency of graph-based applications.

Schools assign summer projects to students with the goal of promoting continuous learning during the summer break from the regular academic schedule. However, there is debate around whether these projects should be teacher-designed or student-designed. I believe summer projects are most beneficial when they allow for student design and choice. When students have autonomy in choosing their own summer project topics, it fosters greater engagement and motivation to learn. Students will naturally be more interested in subjects they personally find intriguing rather than topics handed down from a teacher. This interest keeps students invested in their work over the summer months. It also encourages skills like self-directed learning, time management and independent research - valuable abilities for both school and lifelong learning. Furthermore, student-designed projects can explore areas of learning beyond the standard curriculum. This opens up opportunities forstudents to nurture individual passions and creative strengths. One student may decide to study other cultures and learn basic phrases in foreign languages that interest them, while another interviews family members about their history for a genealogy project. The diversity of these self-guided explorations enriches the learning experience for each student. Of course, teachers can still provide guidance to ensure student-designed projects have academic merit. Suggesting topics, approving proposals, and setting deadlines keep students on track without limiting their autonomy. The structure of teacher expectations combined with student freedom of choice seems to strike the ideal balance for beneficial summer learning. In conclusion, when the goal is engaged and meaningful learning over the summer break, students themselves should have agency in deciding the direction of their projects. This empowers independent learning tailored to each student's interests and learning style. Overall, a student-designed approach to summer work is most effective for promoting continuous academic growth outside of the regular school year.

Once upon a time just after high school, I managed a Radio Shack. I can't speak specifically to the wholesale cost of things like consoles and video games since we didn't carry them in store, but I'm familiar with the markup on basic consumer electronics. If a console is anything like a new TV or stereo, the store isn't turning a huge profit on it. We had maybe a 10-15 margin on something like a new TV. The real profit was always in accessories, especially anything with a Radio Shack brand on it. Say you buy a new TV but also pick up a pack of batteries, a surge protector, and an HDMI cable. Those accessories you just bought made the store more of a profit than the TV. Something like a pack of batteries might be marked up 500 or more. You also bought a protection plan? Even better. In the grand scheme of overall business profitability, even if you eventually have to sell certain items for less than they cost you, you can make it up elsewhere. Some people would come in to the store multiple times to drool over an expensive item without buying. Each time though they might leave with 1 or 2 inexpensive items. Multiply that across a dozen such people who are "just looking" and profits start adding up because people are still buying items on which there are huge profit margins. So ultimately, if a new model of something is coming out and I need to drop the price on the old one to get it sold, it's not that big of a deal because it's more than made up for it by driving foot traffic into the store.

Introduction Impact investing has emerged as a powerful tool for addressing social challenges around the world. By definition, impact investments are made into companies, organizations, or funds with the intention of generating both financial returns and positive social or environmental outcomes. This approach to investment seeks to create long-term value not only for investors but also for society at large. As more individuals and institutions recognize the potential of impact investing to drive meaningful change, its role in addressing pressing social issues continues to grow. This paper will explore the various ways in which impact investing can contribute to solving some of today’s most pressing social problems. One significant area where impact investing can make a difference is poverty alleviation. According to the World Bank, over 700 million people live below the international poverty line of $1.90 per day. While traditional aid programs have played a crucial role in providing relief to those living in extreme poverty, they often fail to promote sustainable economic growth or empower local communities to break free from cycles of poverty. Impact investing offers an alternative approach that prioritizes both financial viability and social impact, enabling investors to support businesses and initiatives that directly benefit low-income populations. For example, microfinance institutions provide small loans to entrepreneurs who lack access to formal banking services, helping them establish or expand their businesses and generate income. Similarly, investments in affordable housing projects can improve living conditions for low-income families while delivering stable returns to investors.

The event calculus is a logical language for representing and reasoning about events and their effects first presented by Robert Kowalski and Marek Sergot in 1986. It was extended by Murray Shanahan and Rob Miller in the 1990s. Similar to other languages for reasoning about change, the event calculus represents the effects of actions on fluents. However, events can also be external to the system. In the event calculus, one can specify the value of fluents at some given time points, the events that take place at given time points, and their effects.

Title: The Face on Mars The Red Planet, Mars, is known for its unique features and mysteries. One such mystery is a geological structure resembling a face, which has sparked the interest of many people, especially space enthusiasts. This formation, known as the Face on Mars, has been subject to various theories, discussions, and even conspiracy theories over the years. The Face on Mars is located near the Martian equator on a section of the Cydonia Mensae region. It is approximately 0.7 miles long and can be seen from a satellite orbiting the planet. This formation was first observed by NASA's Viking 1 Orbiter, which captured images of it in 1976. The Face is a mesa, a flat-topped rock formation, that is approximately 1,500 feet tall and 1,500 feet wide. The Face's resemblance to a human face has been the subject of intense debate among researchers and the public. Many people have suggested that the formation could have been created naturally, while others believe it might be an alien-built monument. However, scientists have found that the most likely explanation is that the Face on Mars is a geological formation resulting from erosion by wind, water, and other natural forces over millions of years. The erosion process on Mars has shaped the landscape in a way that it appears as a face from some angles. The wind has sculpted the mesa over time, and its appearance has been further enhanced due to the presence of shadows and lighting. In conclusion, the Face on Mars is a remarkable geological feature, but it is most likely the result of natural processes rather than an alien-made structure. While it may appear to resemble a human face from some angles, it is essential to consider the scientific explanations and evidence before jumping to conclusions about extraterrestrial involvement. As our knowledge of Mars continues to evolve, we will likely uncover more fascinating discoveries and understand the true nature of the Face on Mars.

One of the primary reasons given is the potential scientific discovery that could be made through Venus exploration. As the author notes, Venus is highly analogous to Earth in since and composition, yet its atmosphere and surface conditions have diverged dramatically due to a greenhouse effect gone haywire. By studying Venus up close, scientists could gain novel insights into climate processes and warn of potential worst case scenarios on Earth. This promise of scientific advancement weighs heavily in favor of accepting the risks. However, the author is also realistic about said risks. Venus's 96% carbon dioxide atmosphere and surface temperatures hot enough to melt lead present clear obstacles. Even short term probes would need protection from this crushing environment. Yet the article outlines thoughtful proposed mission designs, such as aerial and aerial platforms, that could survive for meaningful periods to carry out valuable observations. Drivers Should Not Use Cell Phones While Operating a Vehicle Cell phone use while driving has become an epidemic in today's world. With the rise of smartphones, it is more tempting than ever for drivers to check emails, texts, and social media while on the road. However, the dangers of distracted driving from cell phone use are clear. Numerous studies have shown that drivers who use their phones, even with hands-free technology, have slower reaction times, are less aware of their surroundings, and are more likely to crash. For these reasons, drivers should not be able to use cell phones in any capacity while operating a moving vehicle. Texting while driving in particular is extremely dangerous as it takes a driver's eyes off the road for prolonged periods of time. Texting leads to a 400% increase in time spent not looking at the road. Even short distractions can have catastrophic consequences at high speeds. Every day, around nine people are killed and more than 1,000 injured in crashes that involved distracted driving. The risks of even hands-free calling are unacceptable when human lives are at stake with each drive. Banning all cell phone use, including hands-free, while driving sends a consistent message that operating a vehicle demands a driver's full attention. Partial bans are confusing and hard to enforce. Drivers may still feel permitted to check notifications or have brief conversations even if hands-on use is forbidden. Laws should not just discourage the most dangerous behaviors like texting, but target the root cause of distraction. A studies even show that driving performance is impacted for several minutes after use of voice-command dialing or hands-free modes due to delayed cognitive distraction. In an increasingly wireless world, it may seem restrictive to ban all cell phone activity behind the wheel. However, public safety must come before personal convenience. As vehicles became more complex with added infotainment and connectivity features, distraction risks will only increase without comprehensive bans that futureproof road safety. For the protection of all citizens that share the roads each day, no cell phone use of any kind should be permitted while operating a motor vehicle. Lives depend on drivers paying complete attention to the critical task of navigating traffic safely. A total cell phone ban achieves that goal most effectively.

In essence, human teachers possess the ability to recognize and respond to student emotions effectively, without the need for invasive technological intrusion. Additionally, FACS technology raises concerns regarding individual privacy. Students' emotional states could be subject to invasive monitoring, potentially exacerbating distress. The article highlights that emotions can result from personal experiences and that scrutinizing private emotional states could be a violation of privacy in the context of a school environment. Lastly, the practical and financial costs outweigh the benefits of using this technology. Personalized emotion-detecting computers require constant adaptation, which could disrupt other student's learning experiences, rendering this approach ineffective. Moreover, the financial implications of providing each student with an emotion-sensing system would be substantial and unachievable for most institutions. Therefore, the use of technology such as FACS to identify and interpret emotions is a fascinating development. However, I argue, that when considering its application in classrooms, the potential benefits do not outweigh potential costs, including privacy invasion and inefficiencies in the learning environment. Instead, educators should maintain the use of human-centered approaches and be aware of technology's limitations to preserve individual student privacy.

If aliens deliberately constructed a giant face, they likely would have included distinctive facial characteristics rather than leaving a vague outline open to various interpretations. Splits and dividends can both affect the price of options. A stock split is when a company increases the number of its outstanding shares by issuing more shares to its existing shareholders. This is typically done to make the stock more affordable for individual investors. For example, if a company does a 2-for-1 stock split, it means that each shareholder will receive an additional share for every share they already own. The value of each individual share will be halved as a result of the split, but the total value of the shareholder's holdings will remain the same.Dividends are payments made by a company to its shareholders out of its profits. When a company declares a dividend, it usually reduces the value of its stock by an amount equal to the dividend per share. For example, if a company's stock is trading at $100 per share and it declares a $1 per share dividend, the stock price will typically fall to $99 per share.Both stock splits and dividends can affect the price of options in different ways. For example, if a company does a stock split, the number of shares underlying the options will increase, which will typically cause the price of the options to decrease. On the other hand, if a company declares a dividend, the value of the underlying stock will fall by an amount equal to the dividend, which will typically cause the price of call options to decrease and the price of put options to increase.It's important to note that the effect of a split or dividend on the price of options will depend on the specific terms of the options and the market conditions at the time. It's always a good idea to consult with a financial advisor or professional before making any decisions about how to trade options in the wake of a split or dividend.

A software agent is a program that performs a specific task or set of tasks on behalf of a user or another program. Software agents are designed to be autonomous and operate independently from their user or the system on which they are running. They are often used to automate tasks, gather and analyze data, or perform other functions that would be time-consuming or difficult for a human to do. Software agents can be implemented in many different ways, and can be used for a wide range of applications. Some common examples of software agents include: Web crawlers: These are programs that scan the internet and gather data from websites. Spambots: These are programs that are used to send spam emails or messages. Personal assistants: These are programs that help users manage their schedules and tasks, or provide other types of assistance. Monitoring agents: These are programs that monitor the performance of a system or network and alert the user if there are any problems. Software agents can be implemented in a variety of programming languages, and can be run on a variety of platforms, including desktop computers, servers, and mobile devices. They can be designed to work with a wide range of software and hardware, and can be integrated into other systems or applications.

The Internet has revolutionized the way we live, work, and communicate. It has made the world a smaller place, and it has given us access to an unprecedented amount of information. But how did the Internet come to be? What was its original purpose? And how has it evolved over time? The history of the Internet can be traced back to the early days of computer networking. In the 1960s, researchers at the United States Department of Defense developed a network called ARPANET. ARPANET was designed to be a decentralized network, meaning that no single point of failure could take down the entire network. This made ARPANET very resilient, and it quickly became the backbone of the early Internet. In the 1970s, ARPANET was opened up to researchers at universities and other institutions. This led to the development of new protocols and applications, such as email and the World Wide Web. The World Wide Web was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989, and it quickly became the most popular way to access information on the Internet. In the 1990s, the Internet was commercialized. This led to a boom in the dot-com industry, and it also made the Internet accessible to the general public. By the end of the 1990s, the Internet had become a global phenomenon. Today, the Internet is an essential part of our lives. We use it to stay connected with friends and family, to do our jobs, to learn new things, and to be entertained. The Internet has changed the world in many ways, and it will continue to change the world in the years to come. Here are some of the key events in the history of the Internet: * 1969: ARPANET is created. * 1971: Email is invented. * 1983: TCP/IP is adopted as the standard protocol for the Internet. * 1989: The World Wide Web is invented. * 1993: The Mosaic web browser is released. * 1995: The Internet is commercialized. * 1998: Google is founded. * 2004: Facebook is founded. * 2007: The iPhone is released. * 2010: The iPad is released. * 2012: Google Glass is released. * 2015: The Apple Watch is released. The Internet has come a long way in a short amount of time. It is hard to imagine life without it, and it will be interesting to see how it continues to evolve in the years to come.

The ethical implications of gene editing in humans are a topic of much debate and discussion. As science advances and technology becomes more sophisticated, gene editing has become an increasingly viable option for altering the genetic makeup of humans. However, this raises a number of important questions and concerns about the potential consequences of such technology. One of the most significant ethical implications of gene editing is the potential for creating "designer babies." While this may seem like a positive development, it also raises concerns about the commodification of human life and the potential for creating a society in which people are seen as products rather than individuals. Additionally, there are concerns about the potential for gene editing to be used for eugenics purposes, with the aim of creating a "superior" race. Another major concern is the potential for gene editing to be used for non-therapeutic purposes, such as enhancing athletic performance or creating individuals with specific traits. This raises questions about the boundaries between therapy and enhancement, and whether it is appropriate to use gene editing for non-medical purposes. Furthermore, there are concerns about the potential for gene editing to have unintended consequences, such as creating new diseases or genetic disorders. While gene editing has the potential to cure many genetic diseases, it also has the potential to create new ones. This raises questions about the potential risks and benefits of gene editing, and whether the potential benefits are worth the potential risks. Finally, there are concerns about the potential for gene editing to be used for military purposes, such as creating super-soldiers. While this may seem like the stuff of science fiction, it is a real possibility given the advances in gene editing technology. This raises questions about the potential for gene editing to be used for military purposes, and whether this is an appropriate use of the technology. In conclusion, the ethical implications of gene editing in humans are complex and multifaceted. While gene editing has the potential to revolutionize medicine and improve the lives of many individuals, it also raises important questions and concerns about the potential consequences of the technology. As such, it is important that we continue to debate and discuss these issues in order to ensure that gene editing is used in a responsible and ethical manner.

The Facial Action Coding System (FACS) is a groundbreaking technology that enables computers to recognize and interpret human emotions. As discussed in the article "Making Mona Lisa Smile," this technology has the potential to revolutionize various fields, including education. However, the question remains as to whether FACS is effective in interpreting the emotional expressions of students in a classroom setting. On the one hand, FACS has the potential to enhance the learning experience for students. By using computers equipped with FACS, teachers could adapt their teaching methods in real-time to maintain student engagement. For instance, if a student appears confused or bored, the computer could alert the teacher, who could then adjust their teaching methods to better meet the student's needs. This could lead to a more personalized and effective learning experience for students. On the other hand, there are several concerns regarding the efficacy of FACS in classrooms. Firstly, the technology may not be able to accurately interpret the emotional expressions of students. The human brain is capable of complex emotional calculations, and it is unclear whether FACS can replicate this capacity. Additionally, students may not always express their emotions through facial expressions, making it difficult for computers to accurately detect their emotions. Another concern is the potential invasion of privacy that FACS poses. The use of emotion detection technology in classrooms could lead to unwarranted scrutiny of students' private emotional states. This could be particularly problematic in diverse classroom settings, where students may bring a range of personal experiences and emotions that are not directly related to the classroom environment. Furthermore, the implementation of FACS in classrooms raises practical concerns. The cost of equipping computers with FACS technology would be significant, and it is unclear whether this investment would be worthwhile. In group settings, constant adaptation to individual students' needs could disrupt the learning process for other students. In conclusion, while FACS has the potential to enhance the learning experience for students, its efficacy in interpreting the emotional expressions of students in a classroom setting is uncertain. The potential invasion of privacy and practical concerns surrounding its implementation suggest that a more human-centric approach to education may be more effective. As technology continues to advance, it is crucial to remember the importance of human connection and understanding in education. By embracing a human-centric approach, we can create learning environments that are both effective and respectful of students' privacy.

Humanity has long looked to the stars, seeking intelligence there to match our own. We were never sure if there was even anything out there, but we looked nonetheless. It was on the third of March, 2047 that this question was finally answered. A massive alien ship crash-landed in the middle of the sahara desert. The site was swarmed by news crews, military, science crews - anyone you could think of. It was hours before the first alien emerged from the ship, and upon his exit the alien was immediately bombarded with questions - but it didn't answer: it just went about effecting repairs to the ship, and anything in its' way was gently pushed aside. At first we assumed it was language difficulty. So, we tried more languages. We used pictograms, every form of written communication in the book, every spoken language, we wrote mathematical constants and equations - anything that might reach it. In desparation we even tried explosions to catch its' attention, but they were simply ignored - seemingly nothing could harm it. More aliens emerged from the ship to assist with repairs, and each was asked the same questions, shown the same barrage. We began to grow more and more creative: radio waves, midrowaves, gamma radiation bursts, statuary. We even brought in buddhist monks to meditate in their general direction! But still, nothing. Not a peep, not a glance, nothing. Finally, the aliens finished their business and got back in their ship. Just as the last was entering, one of the men who had been directing the operation screamed, at the top of his lungs, "Why won't you answer us, damnit?" The alien turned, and in one moment ended our dreams forever. Eight words. That was all it took. Scientific funding withered and died, space exploration was given up on. It was the end of our great shining hopes for the future. Those eight words? "Humans were, are, and shall forever remain irrelevant."

Having dealt with with Social Security, state agencies, and banks more than I'd care to, I would urge you to do the following: 1) Get a 100% clear answer on whether or not you are listed as "joint" or "authorized user/signer" for an account. This will probably require a call to the bank, but for less than an hour of you and your friend's time you will save yourself a whole lot of hassle. The difference is like this: if you worked at a business that added you as an authorized user for a credit or debit card, this would allow you to use the card to buy things. But that doesn't make the money in the bank yours! On the other hand if you are listed as "joint", this regards ownership, and it could become tricky to establish whether its your money or not to any governmental satisfaction. 2) You are completely correct in being honest with the agency, but that's not enough - if you don't know what the facts are, you can't really be honest with them. If the form is unclear it's ok to ask, "on having a bank account, does being listed as an authorized user on someone else's account count if it isn't my money or bank account?" But if you are listed as holding the account jointly, that changes the question to: "I am listed as joint on someone else's checking account, but it isn't my money - how is that considered?" To Social Security it might mean generating an extra form, or it might mean you need to have the status on the account changed, or they might not care. But if you don't get the facts first, they won't give you the right answers or help you need. And from personal experience, it's a heck of a lot easier to get a straight and clear answer from a bank than it is from a federal government agency. Have the facts with you when you contact them and you'll be ok - but trust me, you don't want them guessing!

As data sets continue to increase in size and multi-core computer architectures are developed, asynchronous parallel optimization algorithms become more and more essential to the field of Machine Learning. Unfortunately, conducting the theoretical analysis asynchronous methods is difficult, notably due to the introduction of delay and inconsistency in inherently sequential algorithms. Handling these issues often requires resorting to simplifying but unrealistic assumptions. Through a novel perspective, we revisit and clarify a subtle but important technical issue present in a large fraction of the recent convergence rate proofs for asynchronous parallel optimization algorithms, and propose a simplification of the recently introduced "perturbed iterate" framework that resolves it. We demonstrate the usefulness of our new framework by analyzing three distinct asynchronous parallel incremental optimization algorithms: Hogwild (asynchronous Sgd), Kromagnon (asynchronous Svrg) and Asaga , a novel asynchronous parallel version of the incremental gradient algorithm Saga that enjoys fast linear convergence rates. We are able to both remove problematic assumptions and obtain better theoretical results. Notably, we prove that Asaga and Kromagnon can obtain a theoretical linear speedup on multi-core systems even without sparsity assumptions. We present results of an implementation on a 40-core architecture illustrating the practical speedups as well as the hardware overhead. Finally, we investigate the overlap constant, an ill-understood but central quantity for the theoretical analysis of asynchronous parallel algorithms. We find that it encompasses much more complexity than suggested in previous work, and often is order-of-magnitude bigger than traditionally thought.

In the Hesiodic Catalogue of Women, Graecus is presented as the son of Zeus and Pandora II, sister of Hellen the patriarch of Hellenes. Hellen was the son of Deucalion who ruled around Phthia in central Greece. The Parian Chronicle mentions that when Deucalion became king of Phthia, the previously called Graikoi were named Hellenes. Aristotle notes that the Hellenes were related with GraiGreeks (Meteorologica I.xiv) a native name of a Dorian tribe in Epirus which was used by the Illyrians. He also claims that the great deluge must have occurred in the region around Dodona, where the Selloi dwelt. However, according to the Greek tradition it is more possible that the homeland of the Greeks was originally in central Greece. A modern theory derives the name Greek (Latin Graeci) from Graikos, "inhabitant of GraiaGraea," a town on the coast of Boeotia. Greek colonists from Graia helped to found Cumae (900 BC) in Italy, where they were called Graeces. When the Romans encountered them they used this name for the colonists and then for all Greeks (Graeci.) The word graia "old woman" comes from the PIE root gerh2-greh2-, "to grow old" via Proto-Greek gera-grau-iu; the same root later gave geras (keras), "gift of honour" in Mycenean Greek. The Germanic languages borrowed the word Greeks with an initial "k" sound which probably was their initial sound closest to the Latin "g" at the time (Goth. Kreks). The area out of ancient Attica including Boeotia was called Graike and is connected with the older deluge of Ogyges, the mythological ruler of Boeotia. The region was originally occupied by the Minyans who were autochthonous or Proto-Greek speaking people. In ancient Greek the name Ogygios came to mean "from earliest days."

The heart of an engine is the cylinders and pistons. This is where the fuel is burned and converted into mechanical energy and heat. All the other parts of the car, such as the transmission, drive shafts and wheels are powered by this same mechanism. In both cases, it was the exact design that led to a 100 efficiency with gasoline engines in cars until after World War II (and then diesel). The reason for this superiority lay in simple physics: each piston only needs one channel through which its combustion products can be released from the cylinder - regardless of whether you're burning gas or diesel! It's also important not to confuse efficiency with power. In electric motors, we measure efficiency in terms of watts per kilogram of mass moved. If all the weight of the car were in steel, then every watt could move 1 kg. With our car battery, on the other hand, we need to take into account density and the size and shape of those elements relative to our vehicle dimensions - along with any materials used within them - before measuring their power output. Electric vehicles have another advantage over internal-combustion models. A typical compact sedan will weigh around 3,000 pounds. That means the batteries can pack more potential energy than a comparable sized gasoline engine would. Yet these batteries tend to hold less charge capacity because they don't carry extra space to store additional juice! Given that most people start out driving looking forward rather than backwards when it comes to speed, range and cost, why buy anything but a plug-in? Anyway, if your electric car has enough range and does everything else that a comparable model wouldn't do so much better at half the price...why go anywhere near a gas station anyway?!

Small states are essentially ignored, as their electoral votes are effectively guaranteed to one party or the other. I believe that the Electoral College is an outdated and undemocratic system that needs to be abolished. I urge you to support a national popular vote for president. In conclusion, graduating high school a year early has both benefits and drawbacks. Predicting the relevance between two given videos with respect to their visual content is a key component for content-based video recommendation and retrieval. Thanks to the increasing availability of pre-trained image and video convolutional neural network models, deep visual features are widely used for video content representation. However, as how two videos are relevant is task-dependent, such off-the-shelf features are not always optimal for all tasks. Moreover, due to varied concerns including copyright, privacy and security, one might have access to only pre-computed video features rather than original videos. We propose in this paper feature re-learning for improving video relevance prediction, with no need of revisiting the original video content. In particular, re-learning is realized by projecting a given deep feature into a new space by an affine transformation. We optimize the re-learning process by a novel negative-enhanced triplet ranking loss. In order to generate more training data, we propose a new data augmentation strategy which works directly on frame-level and video-level features. Extensive experiments in the context of the Hulu Content-based Video Relevance Prediction Challenge 2018 justify the effectiveness of the proposed method and its state-of-the-art performance for content-based video relevance prediction.

This makes the work feel less like a chore and more like a chance for self directed learning. Students may end up learning more than if given a prescribed assignment since they have motivation to explore topics that light their inner fire. Giving choices also acknowledges that students have diverse strengths, backgrounds and interests. Not every student excels in the same subjects or learns best through identical tasks. Open ended projects respect these differences and let students pursue their natural inclinations and talents. In contrast, rigid teacher assignments neglect the fact that one side does not fit all when it comes to student engagement. While teachers can provide guidance on requirements, allowing space for student ideas ensures projects don't become dull assignments but stimulating summer adventures. It instills accountability as students must self manage their tasks. Overall, self directed projects empower students, fostering skills like independence, time management and lifelong learning—all of which better serve students in the long run compared to following directives over summer. For these reasons, I believe summer projects are best designed by the students themselves rather than teachers.

Rhe use of facial recognition technology like the Facial Action boding System to identify student emotions in the classroom could provide both benefits and drawbacks. Proponents of using this technology argue that it gives teachers valuable insights into how students are reacting to lessons. If a teacher knows that most of the class looks confused or bored during a particular part of a lesson, that indicates that area needs more explanation or a different approach. Rhis data could help teachers tailor their instruction methods to better meet student needs and maximize learning. It may also help identify students who are struggling emotionally but not speaking up, so teachers can check in and offer support. However, there are also reasonable concerns about privacy and the potential misreading of expressions. Bonstant monitoring of student facial expressions during class could be seen as invasive or create extra pressure and self consciousness for students. Facial reactions are also complex and contextual the same expression may signify different emotions depending on the situation. Without understanding context, there is a risk technology could incorrectly interpret a student's emotional state. Bonsent would also be an issue, as most students likely did not sign up to have their facial data collected and analyzed during school. Overall, using facial recognition technology in the classroom deserves careful consideration. While it aims to provide useful insights, schools must weigh student privacy concerns and ensure systems are implemented ethically with appropriate safeguards. More research is also needed to understand how accurately these systems can interpret emotion in real classroom settings with all the variable social contexts involved. Used judiciously and combined with teacher judgment, this technology may help some students, but overly relying on data alone risks misinterpreting the human experience of learning. With open discussion and input from students and parents, schools can decide if the benefits outweigh the drawbacks for their community.

In this paper, joint transceiver design for dual-hop amplify-and-forward (AF) MIMO relay systems with Gaussian distributed channel estimation errors in both two hops is investigated. Due to the fact that the channel estimation errors can have a significant impact on the performance of the system, it is important to take them into account in the joint transceiver design. The proposed design approach considers the use of a linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) estimator to mitigate the channel estimation errors in both hops. The LMMSE estimator is used to estimate the channel matrices at the relay node and the destination node, based on the received signal at the relay node. Using the estimated channel matrices, a joint transceiver design is proposed to optimize the overall system performance in terms of the achievable rate. The proposed design approach involves the joint optimization of the transmit precoding matrices at the source node, the relay node and the destination node, as well as the receive precoding matrices at the relay node and the destination node. Simulation results show that the proposed joint transceiver design approach with channel estimation error mitigation outperforms the non-joint transceiver design approaches and provides significant improvements in the achievable rate, particularly in scenarios where the channel estimation errors are large.

Body, Health and Illness in Popular Culture Essay Popular culture has the capacity to influence and affect the views society holds on a wide range of real-life concepts. The power the media holds over the exchange of information is largely attributed to its ability to shape ideas, perceptions and expectations through stories and narrative tropes. The topics of body, health and illness are no exceptions from this popular rule, as the topic of human relationship with one’s flesh has historically been a subject of interest. In literature, particularly the somewhat older one written in religious societies, illness is often perceived as a sign of supernatural intervention or divine punishment. In ancient Greek canon, oftentimes a character struck by sudden disease has displeased a god and has gotten sick in retribution. Alternatively, the sickness may come from the influence of a negative supernatural creature, such as a witch or a demon, that exists in the direct opposition to the divine. Specific illnesses, however, have received a more complex metaphorical approaches in modern or comparatively recent popular media. If a diagnosis is socially stigmatized, it transforms into horror narratives in cinema and writing. The HIV epidemic might be used as a relevant example, with the real-life repercussions of the diagnosis involving social isolation and prejudice (Kilty & Bogosavljevic, 2018). The marginalizing and often sexual nature of the virus has manifested in HIV-specific cinematographic metaphors that often-involved transformations into a monster. Finally, the human body itself is often portrayed in fiction metaphorically, through a lens of analogy. Mechanical comparisons are largely common, with an organism being represented in the form of a machine. Following the metaphor, different parts of the body might be compared to cogs or other technical elements. And, within this logic, an illness is akin to a breach that needs to be repaired for the mechanism to function. Reference Kilty, J., & Bogosavljevic, K. (2018). Emotional storytelling: Sensational media and the creation of the HIV sexual predator. Crime, Media, Culture: An International Journal , 15 (2), 279-299. Web.

In probability theory and statistics, the multivariate normal distribution, multivariate Gaussian distribution, or joint normal distribution is a generalization of the one-dimensional (univariate) normal distribution to higher dimensions. Respecting others and considering their feelings is crucial for personal and professional success. It is important to remember that our actions and attitudes towards those around us can have a profound impact on the relationships we build, as well as our own well-being. One of the primary reasons why treating people with respect, regardless of age, country, or religion, is essential to succeeding in life is that it fosters a sense of unity and mutual understanding. When we show respect for others, we acknowledge their dignity and value, which in turn encourages them to do the same for us. This creates a positive feedback loop that promotes cooperation and collaboration, both in personal relationships and in professional settings. Moreover, respecting others' feelings and opinions is essential for building strong and lasting connections. People are more likely to trust and confide in those who make them feel valued and understood. By taking the time to listen to someone's perspective and empathize with their emotions, we can create deeper and more meaningful relationships. This not only benefits the individuals involved, but also the overall dynamic of the group or community. In contrast, a lack of respect for others can lead to negative outcomes. When we fail to consider someone's feelings or ignore their needs, we create a barrier between us and that person. This can lead to resentment, conflict, and a breakdown in communication. Furthermore, people who are consistently disrespected may feel undervalued and overlooked, which can lead to decreased motivation and productivity. Our attitude towards the people around us can have a significant impact on our own well-being as well. When we treat others with respect and kindness, we create a positive environment that fosters personal growth and self-esteem. Conversely, a negative or disrespectful attitude can lead to feelings of guilt, anxiety, and depression. In conclusion, it is essential to treat people with respect, regardless of age, country, or religion, in order to succeed in life. By considering others' feelings, building strong relationships, and promoting a positive environment, we can create a more harmonious and successful existence. It is important to remember that our actions and attitudes towards those around us can lead to beneficial or negative outcomes, and that we have the power to choose the path that leads to success.

Combinatorial games are widely used in finite model theory, constraint satisfaction, modal logic and concurrency theory to characterize logical equivalences between structures. In particular, Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse games, pebble games, and bisimulation games have been studied extensively in the literature. These games are played by two players on two structures, which are assumed to be relational, and one of the players is asked to show that the two structures are equivalent. In this talk we present a new class of combinatorial games called tree-width games, which are played on structures that have some tree-like properties. We define winning strategies in tree-width games, and show that the corresponding equivalences are expressible in first-order logic. We also prove that the corresponding logics are the same as the logics characterized by the first-order Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse, pebble, and bisimulation games.

The system uses two cameras connected through an opticalelectrical interface enabling one camera to acquire an exposure value while the other captures an image. The images captured from each camera are combined to determine whether an area has sufficient illumination to support accurate white balancing. If so, then the information content within the image frames may be accurately calculated and used to adjust for local variations. This technique requires use of two cameras which allows the acquisition of both dark and bright regions simultaneously but does not allow automatic switching between cameras during operation. Dear Principal Smith, I am writing to you regarding the decision about whether to require all students to perform community service. While helping the community is certainly important, I do not think making it mandatory is the best approach. There are a few key reasons for my position. Firstly, requiring community service risks taking away students' freedom to choose how to spend their own time. Not all students have the same interests or passions, and forcing them into volunteer work may foster resentment rather than appreciation for service. Some students need time for other commitments like jobs, sports, or caring for family members. Community service is best when it comes from personal motivation rather than obligation. Secondly, mandatory service may discourage deeper engagement with the causes students work for. When volunteering is a mandatory task to complete rather than a choice, students are less likely to feel invested in the work or understand its importance. Surface level engagements do little to help those in need or build empathy in students. Truly meaningful service stems from a student's own desire to help their community. Instead of making it a requirement, I think a better approach is to promote opportunities for voluntary community service and help students understand why it matters. Recognizing student volunteers with awards or letters of recommendation for college could help inspire others to participate freely. Leading by positive example, like having teachers perform service projects, may do more to create a culture of caring than policies of compulsion. In conclusion, while the intent of required community service is understandable, I do not believe it is the most effective way to encourage students to become engaged, caring citizens. Volunteering done out of personal choice is more likely to make a real difference and stay with students long-term. For these reasons, I do not think it should be mandatory for all students. Please let me know if you would like me to elaborate on any part of my position. Sincerely, [Your name]

The rise of digital culture has had a profound impact on creativity and intellectual property. Digital culture refers to the culture that has emerged as a result of the widespread use of digital technologies and the internet. This culture is characterized by the ease of access to information, the ability to share and collaborate on creative works, and the ability to consume and create digital content. This has allowed for the emergence of new forms of creative expression, such as social media, blogging, and podcasting. However, the rise of digital culture has also had negative impacts on creativity. The ease of access to information and the ability to share and copy digital content has made it easier for individuals to plagiarize and steal intellectual property. This has led to a rise in the number of cases of intellectual property theft, such as the copying of music, movies, and artwork. The rise of digital culture has also had a negative impact on the value of intellectual property. The ease of access to digital content has made it harder for creators to monetize their works, as consumers are more likely to access content for free rather than pay for it. This has led to a decline in the value of intellectual property and has made it harder for creators to earn a living from their works. In conclusion, the rise of digital culture has had both positive and negative impacts on creativity and intellectual property. While it has opened up new opportunities for creative expression and collaboration, it has also made it easier for individuals to steal intellectual property and has devalued the worth of intellectual property. It is important for individuals and governments to work together to find ways to protect intellectual property and ensure that creators are able to earn a living from their works in the digital age.

Instead, they argue that Luther likely sent his theses to the Archbishop of Mainz, Albert von Brandenburg, and circulated it among friends, family, and colleagues. Even though the posting of the Ninety-Five Theses on the door of the Castle Church is widely accepted as fact, the scholars argue that it was not the actual method by which Luther spread his ideas.

When you save your game to the PS2 's memory card , a file is written to some flash memory - just like saving a text document to a USB flash drive . The data in the file is structured - it has specific fields in it that indicate different parts of the saved state of the game . For instance , there might be a section of the file that indicates the maximum health of your character , or whether or not you 've completed a specific quest . When the game goes to load this file off your card , if the data is wrong somehow - the maximum health is off the charts , or your inventory is full of items that do n't exist - then the save file is considered corrupt and ca n't be loaded . Corruption can occur for many reasons . One is that memory is n't always foolproof . Hard drives fail , flash memory can go bad , etc . It was especially bad in the earlier days of flash memory , so GameCube , Playstation , PS2 , etc memory cards were more error prone than the USB keys we use today . The technology has improved somewhat to be more fault tolerant and to work for longer . It 's also possible that the game had a glitch or was turned off while saving , thus writing an invalid or incomplete file to the card . It 's also possible that external conditions could damage the device ( and thus , the file stored on it ) over time . Since there 's typically nothing players can do to recover a corrupted save , the game typically just gives you a generic error and refuses to load the game .

The early 20th century saw immense social upheaval and change, not least of which was the rise of the feminist movement. As women fought for and gained more rights and opportunities, one of the areas most impacted was literature. Female authors gained more opportunities to write and publish their works, and the themes and subjects of literature began to shift to reflect women's experiences. No longer were women confined to the domestic sphere or relegated to being muses for male authors. They emerged as authors in their own right, exploring issues that were important and relevant to them. The 1920s saw the rise of authors like Virginia Woolf, who provided insight into women's interior lives and experiences. Her works like A Room of One's Own tackled issues around women and fiction, arguing that in order for women to produce great works of art they needed space and means of their own. The feminist movement opened up space for women to write about topics that had been taboo or discouraged previously. Sexuality, desire, and women's experiences with their own bodies became subjects authors felt empowered to explore. Works like Kate Chopin's The Awakening provide a glimpse into a woman's sexual and personal awakening in a time when those topics were still quite scandalous. The movement also gave rise to subgenres like lesbian literature, with authors like Radclyffe Hall exploring romantic relationships between women. Poetry also saw enormous changes, with poets like Sylvia Plath producing deeply personal works that provided insight into women's experiences with topics like mental health, motherhood, and trauma. Plath's Ariel in particular is a seminal work, reflecting her own struggles with depression and her turbulent relationship with her father. The rawness and deeply personal nature of much of women's literature in the 20th century was revolutionary and helped establish the precedent that women's experiences were worthy and important subjects for art and literature. The feminist movement opened the door for an outpouring of women's creativity that had previously been stifled. No longer content to be muses or domestic creatures, women emerged as formidable artists in their own right, forever changing the landscape of 20th century literature. They introduced new genres, broke long-held taboos, and helped establish women's experiences as important subjects for literature, creating works that continue to resonate deeply today. The impact of the feminist movement on 20th century literature is deep, vast, and eternal.

This means that, to the person who was not traveling as fast, it would appear as though you had traveled back in time. So, in a way, FTL travel can imply backward time travel because it can make it appear as though you have gone back in time to someone who was not traveling as fast as you. While distance learning has some potential benefits for students, I don't believe it would be as beneficial as traditional unperson classes for most students. One argument in favor of distance learning is that it allows for greater flexibility. Students who have medical issues, family responsibilities, or long commute times could potentially maintain their education from home through online or remote classes. This kind of flexible option may help keep students engaged who otherwise might struggle to attend regular classes. However, I think students would be better served by the traditional classroom experience for several reasons. First, the social interaction that occurs naturally in a classroom setting is important for students' development. Through group projects, class discussions, and informal conversations, students learn valuable collaboration and communication skills they cannot get through a video screen. They also build important social and emotional skills through peer interactions. Additionally, the structure and accountability of unperson classes tends to keep students more engaged and on track. It can be too easy for students learning at home to become distracted or fall behind without the physical presence of a teacher. Distance learning also makes it harder for teachers to give students individual attention and ensure they are comprehending lessons. For these reasons, distance learning may not be the most effective learning environment for many students. In conclusion, while distance learning has its place in providing flexible options, I believe traditional in class instruction remains the superior model for most t12 students. The social and developmental benefits of peer2peer interaction, along with the structure and accountability of physical classrooms, make unperson classes the healthier choice for supporting student success. Distance learning should be considered a supplemental option rather than a full replacement for physical school attendance.

Schools assigning summer projects aim to ensure students continue learning outside the academic year. However, the types of projects given should allow for student choice and interests. Student designed summer projects are preferable to teacher designed ones. Been students have autonomy in choosing their summer work, they are more engaged and motivated to complete quality work. Knowing their interests best, students can pick a project related to a hobby, future career path, or just something they genuinely want to learn more about. Being able to design their own project increases ownership over their learning. In contrast, teacher chosen assignments risk becoming dull homework that is merely checked off a list. Student designed projects also encourage creativity, problem solving and responsibility. By researching topics themselves and planning out their projects, students develop valuable life skills. They must determine feasible goals and timelines for completion. Presenting unique ideas of their own fosters an entrepreneurial approach to learning outside the classroom. On the other hand, following teacher guidelines leaves little room for innovation or customizing projects to individual strengths. While guidelines from teachers help ensure educational merit, the specifics of projects should be up to each student. Having autonomy to design projects tapped into their interests keeps students engaged over summer break. This approach balances student choice with academic expectations better than uniform, teacher directed assignments. Overall, student designed summer work sustains learning while cultivating important independent learning habits that will serve students well in and after school.

Education plays an instrumental role in promoting environmental sustainability. Education is key to shifting society toward more sustainable ways of living that protect and preserve the natural environment. By educating students from an early age about sustainability challenges and solutions, we can shape future generations of environmental stewards. Students can develop the knowledge, skills, and motivation to make positive changes in their own lives and communities. While policy and technology also play important roles, education is the foundation for promoting widespread understanding of why sustainability matters and empowering people to take action. In conclusion, education is essential for promoting environmental sustainability. Educating students about sustainability issues and solutions fosters the knowledge and skills needed to build a healthier planet for ourselves and future generations. Students can become catalysts for change by sharing what they learn with others and taking action in their own lives. Education is key to creating a more sustainable future for all.

We propose a novel mathematical framework to address the problem of automatically solving large jigsaw puzzles. This problem assumes a large image which is cut into equal square pieces that are placed on a grid and faces "multiple" other images, each being cut in the same way as the others but with different orientation. The images may be viewed individually or they can be linked together via links (i.e, by flipping them horizontally). The proposed algorithm uses two main strategies: (1) finding all pairs of connected pieces; (2) finding all consecutive pairs of pieces having the same orientation.
